seed.title: Access Studio: choose a route, keep control
seed.idea: Refine the original library-access workbench into a concrete fictional community-event participation journey. Give a patron a visible mission and a small illustrated route board: explore an event, choose what help to seek, inspect an invented registration requirement and decide a next step. All event details and service responses must be clearly authored examples; the interface never registers anybody. Offer a local mock online route, asking staff to explain a step, taking a complete paper route, and pausing or declining. Let choices visibly change the route, help available and unresolved conditions. Introduce a changed condition such as an unfamiliar account requirement or temporarily unavailable staff; the patron can change route without being labeled deficient. Do not ever ask for a password, name, identifier, email, phone or real account information, even in the mock portal. Mock controls should be task choices, not personal-data fields. End in a reviewable, correctable before/after plan describing a chosen route, control boundary, support needed and a fallback. Patron agency and actual service/staff conditions must be coupled: choosing staff help cannot make staff available. Include a second optional fictional situation with fewer suggestions as supported practice, and a complete paper/facilitation packet. The previous library journal is an immutable parent, not an approved service or measured baseline.
seed.domain: Public library digital participation and community service access
seed.people: Adult patrons with varied reading, languages and device access; librarians, volunteers and service owners; none participate in this demonstration.
seed.constraints: No personal information, credentials, account fields, eligibility advice, banking, legal or medical guidance, patron scoring or deficit labels. No real booking, submissions or external links from the generated candidate. No network, storage, telemetry or external assets. Main path must use concrete route choices, authored consequences and at most two optional open-text fields; never solicit personal detail. Plain language, visual hierarchy with text alternatives, responsive layout, keyboard/focus support, cancel and faithful correction, cover/resume and confirmed complete clearing for shared-device handoff. Put detailed review metadata in Help. Passing, oral assistance, paper and stopping are legitimate choices; do not promise available staff, connectivity, translation or service capacity. Provide complete invented paper materials, not a sentence suggesting paper. The design brief must map relevant roles and proposed task lenses to product requirements, rationale, interactions, acceptance checks and evidence boundaries. Patron/librarian/practitioner review, accessibility/usability, field pilot, learning, transfer and flourishing remain untested. Source preferably below 60000 bytes in file-writing delivery; develop a distinct access journey rather than the school-science interaction.

task_lenses.question: What problem is actually being solved, for whom, and what non-learning explanation could account for it?

task_lenses.name: Coupled requirements and dependencies
task_lenses.question: What must people and the system each be able to do, and which support conditions make their joint performance possible?

task_lenses.name: Practice, feedback and revision
task_lenses.question: What meaningful decision does the learner make, what changes as a consequence, and how can they reconsider it?

task_lenses.name: Interaction design and executable prototyping
task_lenses.question: Which concrete interaction makes the requirement real, and how can a reviewer exercise it?

task_lenses.name: Participation, agency and correction
task_lenses.question: Who controls the tool, whose explanation is represented, and how can people dissent, correct, pass or choose another route?

task_lenses.name: Delegation and accountable decisions
task_lenses.question: Which decisions are supported by the tool, which remain human, and where could the interface imply unjustified authority?

task_lenses.name: Evidence, comparison and inference
task_lenses.question: What task evidence would support or weaken the claim, and what would the available comparison actually establish?

task_lenses.name: Retention and transfer
task_lenses.question: How is immediate supported performance distinguished from later performance in a changed context?

task_lenses.name: Behavioral verification and recovery
task_lenses.question: Which observed interaction confirms the implemented behavior, including failure, correction and recovery?

task_lenses.name: Access, workload and contextual fit
task_lenses.question: What language, device, time, workflow and support conditions make this usable, and who bears the work?

task_lenses.name: Privacy and shared-device boundaries
task_lenses.question: What is visible, retained or disclosed, and what can someone actually control during an interruption or handoff?

design.body:
STATUS AND BASIS
Provisional integrated Design revision for public deliberation in a rehearsal. Sequence 24 integrates the dependency model and retention boundaries; sequence 20 separates supported planning from optional practice and learning inquiry. Sequence 27 supplies a hypothetical keyboard-and-magnification interruption exposing unspecified control placement and focus behavior. No incident, technical success, participant observation, approval or field result is asserted.

REVISION AND SCOPE
Revise Design once: replace nominal reachability with explicit placement, reflow and focus requirements. The dependency model and problem frame remain applicable; the earliest artifact needing this change is Design. The unresolved Understand human-review gate remains pending, without requesting another revision of Understand.

SCREEN ORDER AND ACCESS
Place a short strip labeled “Privacy and stopping” before planning content and first among interactive controls in keyboard order. Use neutral buttons: “Conceal draft,” “Clear draft,” and “Stop exercise.” Keep applicable actions accessible during active, paused, stopped and concealed states; clearing must remain available without revealing content.
The layout must wrap controls without horizontal scrolling, clipping or overlap at magnification settings selected through human review. Any persistent positioning must not obscure controls, focused elements or task content. Review must examine discoverability from within the planning area, not merely from the initial screen. Do not rely on assumed shortcuts, devices or staff intervention. These are requirements to verify, not accessibility claims.

FICTIONAL PLANNING CONTENT
Opening: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Its notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Real routes and assistance availability are unknown. Use fictional choices only.”
Approach choices: consider online; check for paper; check for staffed help; availability unknown; none works; undecided. Next-action choices: examine the notice; ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available; check another route; my action is not listed; undecided. Both default to undecided. No explanation is required for a missing action.
“Describe my draft” optionally presents fixed text describing current selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” Visible descriptions update immediately after correction. No preferred route, praise, score or completion judgment is allowed.

PRIVACY AND FOCUS TRANSITIONS
Conceal hides selectors, descriptions and all choice-specific messages, including interruption output, from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access. Move focus to a neutral status: “Fictional content remains in this session.” Provide explicit reveal, clear and stop controls. Reveal restores visibility only; it must not resume activity automatically or announce a choice-specific summary.
Clear removes candidate-held choices, descriptions and choice-specific messages. Move focus to: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Preserve paused or stopped activity. Do not recreate a draft automatically. A new undecided draft requires explicit action; resuming also requires explicit action. Focus destinations must remain available and understandable without exposing choices.
Use temporary current-draft memory only: no free text, history, analytics, persistent storage, exports, transmissions or automatic staff requests. All implementation boundaries require verification.

OPTIONAL CHANGE AND RECOVERY
Offer separate invitations to try a confusing notice or rehearse an interruption. Neither unlocks assistance or finishing. Confusion repeats that confirmation and help availability remain unresolved. Interruption states: “Imagine the shared-computer session ends before you continue,” and pauses activity. Offer keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; privacy controls remain available. No automatic recovery or inferred intention is permitted. If draft loss is known, disclose it and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices.

NON-AI COMPARISON
Prepare a paper card with the same notice, approach and action choices, correction, uncertainty, pause and stop. Pointing or speaking is sufficient; writing is optional and fictional only. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it; discreet handling needs review. Ordinary conversation with available staff and clearer service notices remain alternatives. Staff capacity is unknown; reviewers may prefer an alternative or reject the tool.

REVIEW AND NEXT ACTION
Prepare this revised screen outline, paper card and fictional transition checks. Proposed checks cover keyboard discovery during interruption, magnified reflow, neutral focus, complete concealment, stale descriptions, clear while stopped, and storage/transmission boundaries. None has been performed.
Accountable patron and librarian review must examine framing, access, privacy, missing actions and workload before approved design. Technical verification and human interaction testing must precede any pilot. Field evidence remains pending. Preserve contrary accounts and reasons for changes. Separate any voluntary learning inquiry using another fictional task and documented support conditions; completion, speed or one revised plan cannot establish retention or transfer.

model.body:
STATUS AND BASIS
Integrated Model artifact for public deliberation in a rehearsal; requirements remain provisional. Sequences 4 and 6 identify service barriers and meaningful refusal. Sequence 8 incorporates those into Understand. Sequence 13 separates plan preference from provision and challenges incomplete concealment. No participant observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. Modeling does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate.

PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY
Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action.

DEPENDENCY MODEL
A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning.

STATE MODEL
Maintain independent fields:
Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided.
Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability.
Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action.
Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion.

REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS
Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan.
Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise.

ADOPTED MODEL REVISION
Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame.

LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK
A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. STATUS AND BASIS
Integrated working artifact for this rehearsal, not human-approved requirements. Sequence 4 identifies route reality, privacy and assistance capacity as unresolved. Sequence 6 challenges the assumption that three offered routes constitute meaningful choice. The seed supplies the fictional task and restrictions. No participant observations, human approvals or field results exist.

PROBLEM FRAME
Investigate what enables adults to choose an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service while retaining control, privacy and manageable effort. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping.

ADOPTED REVISION
The draft interaction must include “availability unknown,” “none works for me,” and “pause or stop,” without requiring a reason. Next actions may be selected, spoken, written or undecided. This changes both the interaction and its review criteria: a finished plan is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of supported choice. These are working requirements awaiting human review, not approved commitments.

FICTIONAL REVIEW MATERIAL
Exercise text: “Imagine a made-up library event called Community Drawing Hour. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Online, paper and staffed routes are possibilities to examine; their real availability is unknown.”

Planning card, usable on paper or as a later screen outline:
• Approach: online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / pause or stop.
• Next action: examine the fictional notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / leave undecided / stop. A different fictional action may be expressed, but writing is optional.
• Change prompt: “The shared computer session ends before you continue, or the instruction remains confusing. Keep, change or abandon your plan.” Do not require recovery or an explanation.
• Feedback example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability remains unknown. You can change or stop this plan.” Feedback describes explicit choices only; it cannot establish access, readiness, consent, skill or transfer.

PRIVACY AND ACCESS BOUNDARIES
Use no real passwords, identifiers, contact details, account information or service records. Concealment must explain that fictional notes remain in the current session. Clearing must remove candidate-held notes and visibly confirm removal; it must not promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Examine what appears after interruption and session ending. Wording, languages, keyboard access and other participation arrangements require review. Paper also needs readable wording, physical access and discreet handling.

COMPARISON AND OPEN QUESTIONS
Compare the candidate with the same paper card and an ordinary conversation with available staff. Review may favor either alternative or reject the workbench. Unknowns include actual route availability, assistance boundaries, staff capacity, language needs, shared-device behavior and whether another planning task is wanted. Preserve objections even if other reviewers favor the candidate.

EVIDENCE PLAN — ALL PENDING
Proposed review questions: Can reviewers identify an acceptable action, including no action? Do route labels imply unavailable provision? Can they revise, conceal, clear and stop with understandable consequences? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens does each approach introduce? Use fictional content only and retain contrary accounts. Difficulty could reflect instructions or unavailable opportunities; apparent ease could reflect prior familiarity. Later transfer would need separate evidence in another fictional task and cannot be inferred from completion here.

NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATE
Prepare the paired paper card and screen outline from these working requirements, plus a route-and-assistance questions sheet. Then arrange patron and librarian review of the problem framing, refusal paths, access arrangements, privacy wording and workload boundaries. Record proposed changes and unresolved dissent without declaring consensus. Advancement requires accountable human review of this framing; any interactive candidate subsequently requires human review and interaction testing before a pilot. No review, launch or efficacy is asserted.

response.artifact_body:
## Problem and people

Expert draft for public deliberation in a rehearsal. No patron, librarian or practitioner has reviewed or approved it. Sequence 2 preserves the parent Understand, Map and Design artifacts as background, including their unresolved human gates and shared-device privacy requirements. Historical sequence labels inside that preserved material are not new evidence for this contribution.

The proposed task is to explore an invented community event, inspect an authored participation requirement and choose an acceptable next step. The people whose interests require review are adult patrons with varied reading, language and device access; librarians and volunteers who may provide assistance; and service owners who control actual event routes. None participate in this demonstration.

D1.problem challenge: difficulty with an account step may reflect an avoidable service requirement, unclear notice or unavailable route. The product must not treat independent online progress as the problem to solve. D5.context challenge: choosing help does not create staff capacity, language assistance, connectivity or time on a shared computer.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: patrons control whether to continue and may respond by selecting, pointing or speaking. Passing and declining require no justification. Librarians define what assistance can reasonably cover; service owners verify real routes before any later service use. Patron and practitioner review must examine whether the proposed task is wanted and understandable.

System requirements: keep preference separate from provision. For this rehearsal, show authored example conditions alongside each route and retain a visible statement that real availability is unknown. Choosing staff help changes the draft support request, not the staff availability state. Choosing paper opens complete invented materials, not a claim that the real service accepts paper.

Authority remains external to the candidate: it cannot register, reserve help, establish eligibility, verify accounts or determine capability. The candidate should use no open-text fields for this task; fixed choices can express its core decisions without inviting personal information.

## Experience and decisions

Opening mission: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Explore its example notice and decide what you would do next. This exercise cannot register anyone. Use only the fictional choices shown.” The small route board has text labels for Explore, Choose a route, Check a condition and Review your plan. Illustrations must carry no information absent from those labels.

Invented notice: “Community Drawing Hour offers a morning session and an afternoon session. Materials are provided in this example. The notice says: ‘Confirm your place.’ The route details below are invented for practice.” Session preference is optional and is not a booking.

Offer a local mock online route, asking staff to explain a step, a complete paper practice route, and pause/decline. Include “No route works for me” and “Leave undecided.” Reveal route details when selected. The online detail says: “This example portal requires an account step before confirmation. No account is created here.” Its controls are Inspect the requirement, Seek an explanation, Change route and Stop; it has no account, credential or contact fields.

The staff route says: “You would ask someone to explain the confirmation step. Real assistance and language support are unknown. No request is sent.” The paper route opens the packet below and says: “These are complete practice materials. Real paper acceptance is unknown.”

Record an initial draft using fixed choices. Invite, without requiring, one authored change: “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit.” If staff help was selected, retain that preference and visibly mark the dependency as unresolved. Offer wait without a promised time, inspect another route, remain undecided or stop. Never silently substitute an online route.

The final descriptive plan shows Before and Now: chosen route, explicit next action, who controls the relevant condition, support needed and fallback. Use “Not chosen” where a field is undecided. Every entry can be corrected; changing an entry replaces its dependent description. The result always says “Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.” No completion rating or ability judgment appears.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Origin: Public library access domain specialist, D1.problem; preserved dependency framing in sequence 2. Pair each route preference with its example condition and unresolved real provision. This prevents an interface choice from implying an available opportunity. Check by selecting staff help and applying the unavailable-staff condition: the preference remains, no assistance is confirmed, and reconsideration is possible without a deficit label.

R2 — Origin: Public library access domain specialist, D1.problem and D5.context; the seed’s unfamiliar-account condition. Any persistent positioning must not obscure controls, focused elements or task content. Review must examine discoverability from within the planning area, not merely from the initial screen. Do not rely on assumed shortcuts, devices or staff intervention. These are requirements to verify, not accessibility claims.

FICTIONAL PLANNING CONTENT
Opening: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Its notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Real routes and assistance availability are unknown. Use fictional choices only.”
Approach choices: consider online; check for paper; check for staffed help; availability unknown; none works; undecided. Next-action choices: examine the notice; ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available; check another route; my action is not listed; undecided. Both default to undecided. No explanation is required for a missing action.
“Describe my draft” optionally presents fixed text describing current selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” Visible descriptions update immediately after correction. No preferred route, praise, score or completion judgment is allowed.

PRIVACY AND FOCUS TRANSITIONS
Conceal hides selectors, descriptions and all choice-specific messages, including interruption output, from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access. Move focus to a neutral status: “Fictional content remains in this session.” Provide explicit reveal, clear and stop controls. Reveal restores visibility only; it must not resume activity automatically or announce a choice-specific summary.
Clear removes candidate-held choices, descriptions and choice-specific messages. Move focus to: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Preserve paused or stopped activity. Do not recreate a draft automatically. A new undecided draft requires explicit action; resuming also requires explicit action. Focus destinations must remain available and understandable without exposing choices.
Use temporary current-draft memory only: no free text, history, analytics, persistent storage, exports, transmissions or automatic staff requests. All implementation boundaries require verification.

OPTIONAL CHANGE AND RECOVERY
Offer separate invitations to try a confusing notice or rehearse an interruption. Neither unlocks assistance or finishing. Confusion repeats that confirmation and help availability remain unresolved. Interruption states: “Imagine the shared-computer session ends before you continue,” and pauses activity. Offer keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; privacy controls remain available. No automatic recovery or inferred intention is permitted. If draft loss is known, disclose it and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices.

NON-AI COMPARISON
Prepare a paper card with the same notice, approach and action choices, correction, uncertainty, pause and stop. Pointing or speaking is sufficient; writing is optional and fictional only. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it; discreet handling needs review. Ordinary conversation with available staff and clearer service notices remain alternatives. Staff capacity is unknown; reviewers may prefer an alternative or reject the tool.

REVIEW AND NEXT ACTION
Prepare this revised screen outline, paper card and fictional transition checks. Proposed checks cover keyboard discovery during interruption, magnified reflow, neutral focus, complete concealment, stale descriptions, clear while stopped, and storage/transmission boundaries. None has been performed.
Accountable patron and librarian review must examine framing, access, privacy, missing actions and workload before approved design. Technical verification and human interaction testing must precede any pilot. Field evidence remains pending. Preserve contrary accounts and reasons for changes. Separate any voluntary learning inquiry using another fictional task and documented support conditions; completion, speed or one revised plan cannot establish retention or transfer.","content_hash":"3f234e938602b268ec8f69c3c64e17b5fad30fe53fda30a65729cd72ee6aa306","revision":2},"model":{"body":"STATUS AND BASIS

PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY
Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action.

DEPENDENCY MODEL
A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning.

STATE MODEL
Maintain independent fields:
Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided.
Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability.
Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action.
Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion.

REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS
Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan.
Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise.

ADOPTED MODEL REVISION
Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame.

LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK
A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed.

NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS
Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. Review may favor an alternative or reject all candidates.

EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES — PENDING
Proposed comparison questions: Can reviewers find an acceptable action, including stopping? Do labels imply provision? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens arise? Can fictional content be corrected, concealed completely and cleared after interruption? Retain contrary accounts and distinguish task familiarity, reviewer prompting and service barriers from any learning explanation. Completion and speed are insufficient evidence.
Unknowns include route existence, staffing windows, language arrangements, accessibility needs, shared-device behavior and demand for this tool. Accountable patron and librarian review must address framing, privacy, access and workload before approved design or a pilot. Subsequent technical checks and human interaction testing remain required. No recruitment, review, launch or efficacy is asserted.

PROBLEM FRAME
Investigate what enables adults to choose an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service while retaining control, privacy and manageable effort. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping.

The draft interaction must include “availability unknown,” “none works for me,” and “pause or stop,” without requiring a reason. Next actions may be selected, spoken, written or undecided. This changes both the interaction and its review criteria: a finished plan is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of supported choice. FICTIONAL REVIEW MATERIAL
Exercise text: “Imagine a made-up library event called Community Drawing Hour. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Online, paper and staffed routes are possibilities to examine; their real availability is unknown.”

Planning card, usable on paper or as a later screen outline:
• Approach: online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / pause or stop.
• Next action: examine the fictional notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / leave undecided / stop. A different fictional action may be expressed, but writing is optional.
• Change prompt: “The shared computer session ends before you continue, or the instruction remains confusing. Keep, change or abandon your plan.” Do not require recovery or an explanation.

response.artifact_body:
## Problem and people

Expert draft for public deliberation in a rehearsal. No requirements here are approved. Sequence 2 preserves the parent Understand, Map and Design records and their unresolved human gates. It is a preservation event, not a new interaction finding. Sequence 5 supplies the current domain proposal, including the fictional event, separate preference and provision, complete paper materials and optional practice.

The task is to inspect the invented Community Drawing Hour notice, consider its authored confirmation requirement and choose an acceptable next step. Adult patrons, librarians, volunteers, service owners and accessibility practitioners have relevant interests; none participate in this demonstration.

D1.problem challenge: an unfamiliar account step may indicate unnecessary service friction, unclear information, language mismatch or unavailable support. More patron training is only one possible response and has no supporting evidence here. An acceptable outcome includes an unresolved plan, paper practice, seeking an explanation when assistance exists, or stopping.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: patrons retain authority over continuing and correcting their choices. Pointing, speaking, passing and declining remain legitimate. Available facilitators may read an authored notice or restate an explicit selection, but must not infer agreement, supply a preferred answer or promise assistance. Librarians and service owners must establish actual service conditions before any later operational use.

System requirements: distinguish the patron's preference, the fictional condition being explored, real provision that remains unknown, and the draft next action. Selecting staff help records a preference; it cannot create a staffed opportunity. Selecting paper practice opens complete invented materials; it cannot establish real paper acceptance. The mock online route may describe an account requirement but must contain no account or credential controls.

The coupling is conditional: a desired action may depend on understandable information, a usable route, device time and suitable assistance. The candidate can expose those dependencies and support reconsideration. It cannot supply missing service capacity. Authority over the event requirement belongs to the service owner; authority over offered assistance belongs to its provider; the patron controls participation in this exercise.

## Experience and decisions

Keep the primary journey short: explore the invented notice, choose a route, inspect one condition and review a draft. Use the four text-labelled route choices proposed in the seed: mock online practice, staff explanation, complete paper practice, and pause/decline. Also permit no workable route and undecided without requiring an explanation. Use fixed controls and no open-text fields for this candidate.

The first review describes the current choice. An optional explicit action, “Keep this as my initial plan,” records a temporary comparison snapshot. Without that action, show “Initial plan not recorded”; do not fabricate a baseline. Invite the authored change, “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit.” Keep the patron's preference and display its unresolved dependency. Offer reconsideration, waiting without a promised duration, remaining undecided or stopping. Never select another route automatically.

The current plan describes route, next action, control boundary, requested support and fallback. It always states “Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.” Changed fields receive descriptive feedback, such as “You changed from staff explanation to paper practice. Real paper acceptance is unknown.” Feedback must derive from explicit choices rather than judge progress.

The optional Neighborhood Story Circle task uses fewer suggestions and its own authored notice. Entering it requires a clear choice to replace the current task, with an opportunity to cancel. It unlocks nothing. Any apparent independence remains uninterpreted until reviewed evidence documents prior familiarity and support.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Dependency honesty. Origin: Systems engineer, D1.coupling; domain specialist at sequence 5; preserved Map dependency separation in sequence 2. Selecting a route must reveal its authored requirement, the party controlling it, real provision marked unknown and an action the patron can choose. Selecting staff explanation must leave staff availability unchanged. Acceptance check: select staff explanation, apply fictional unavailability and inspect the plan; the preference remains visible, the dependency becomes unresolved, no help is confirmed and every other route or refusal remains selectable. Context boundary: the changed condition is hypothetical and actual staffing is unknown.

R2 — Correctable comparison. Origin: Systems engineer, D4.verification; before/after proposal at sequence 5; sequence 2's temporary-memory and correction boundaries. Retain at most an explicitly recorded initial snapshot and the current draft within the active session. Generate descriptions from those selections; do not maintain an accumulating choice log. “Correct initial plan” must be distinct from “Change current plan,” with plain labels explaining which side changes. Acceptance check: record an initial staff preference, change the current route to paper, then correct the initial route to undecided. The comparison must describe those exact states and remove obsolete staff-derived claims. A cleared snapshot must never be reconstructed. Context boundary: before/after comparison is a design intention, not measured reflection or learning.

R3 — Separate privacy, activity and content. Origin: Systems engineer, D1.coupling and D4.verification; domain privacy requirement at sequence 5; preserved focus and concealment requirements in sequence 2. Place Cover, Clear and Stop before task controls in keyboard order. Cover hides every choice-bearing view, including both snapshots, feedback, optional practice and assistance descriptions, from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access. Focus moves to a neutral status. Reveal changes visibility only. Resume is an explicit separate action when activity is paused. Clear remains available while covered or stopped and removes all candidate-held selections and derived task content before confirming its limited scope. It preserves pause or stop and does not create a new draft. Acceptance check: exercise these transitions from an initial/current comparison, a changed-condition view and optional practice; verify neutral focus, no exposed choices while covered, no stale descriptions after clearing and no automatic restart. Context boundary: clearing the candidate does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.

R4 — Recovery without inferred intent. Origin: Systems engineer, D4.verification; sequence 2's interruption and loss boundaries; sequence 5's meaningful refusal. A fictional interruption pauses activity without changing route preference. Cancel closes a pending route change, task replacement or clear confirmation without modifying choices. If the page is reloaded, temporary task state is lost: the opening explains that no prior draft is restored and offers a fresh undecided task, paper materials or stopping. Acceptance check: cancel each pending action, interrupt a changed plan, then reload; unchanged choices survive cancellation, interruption does not silently resume, and reload restores no selections. Context boundary: no persistent storage or recovery history is permitted; these checks have not been executed.

R5 — Equivalent non-AI task and feasible support. Origin: Systems engineer, D1.problem and D1.coupling; domain packet at sequence 5; paper comparison and workload concerns preserved in sequence 2. Make the complete paper packet available before any digital choice. The packet must carry the same authored requirement, changed condition, initial/current choices, control boundary, correction and refusal. Oral assistance is conditional on an actually available person. Acceptance check: a reviewer can conduct the fictional decision using only the packet, without opening the digital route or supplying personal information; the facilitator can restate a corrected choice without selecting an answer. Context boundary: printing, physical access, language arrangements and handling effort need practitioner and affected-person review.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

The initial/current comparison makes a changed decision inspectable but adds state and wording. Keep it optional, retain only two temporary snapshots and show expanded explanations on request. Correctability matters more than filling every field.

Preserve dissent that a planning tool may be unnecessary. A clearer notice, verified route information or removal of a needless account step could address the barrier at its source. Complete paper practice and an ordinary conversation with available staff are non-AI options. None establishes operational service access.

Complete invented paper/facilitation packet for this state design:

Card A — Mission and notice. “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon sessions and says ‘Confirm your place.’ Choose a possible next step; you are not registering. Point, speak, mark, pass, pause or stop. Use no personal information.”

Card B — Route conditions. “Online practice: inspect an invented account requirement; do not create an account or supply details. Staff explanation: ask someone to explain a step if suitable assistance exists; real availability and language support are unknown. Paper practice: use these cards; real acceptance of paper is unknown. No workable route and undecided are valid choices.”

Card C — Initial plan, optional. “Route: online practice / staff explanation / paper practice / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect requirement / seek explanation if assistance exists / examine another route / wait without a promised time / pause / stop / undecided. Support wanted: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: examine another route / remain undecided / pause / stop.” Record only if wanted. No written reason is required.

Card D — Changed condition. “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Your preference does not make assistance available. Keep it unresolved, reconsider a route, wait without a promised duration, pause or stop.”

Card E — Current plan and correction. Repeat Card C's choices for the current plan. “The service owner controls the requirement; assistance providers control what help they offer; you control continuing. Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.” Correct the initial or current selection explicitly, or leave either blank. The facilitator restates the selected side and accepts correction without asking for justification.

Card F — Handling and facilitation. “Covering or folding cards conceals them; it does not erase them. Before marking, agree how cards will be handled. Stop or pass without explanation.” Facilitator script: “Would you like to point, speak, mark, pass or stop? Shall I read the notice? Which route, if any? Here is the imagined change. Keep or change your choice? Which plan should I correct?” Do not record personal information, infer understanding or promise service support.

Optional practice card — “Neighborhood Story Circle is invented. Its notice says ‘Check joining arrangements.’ Use Cards B, C and E to choose a next step. Imagine shared-computer time ends. Keep, revise, pause or stop.” Offer extra prompts only if requested; document their use in any later reviewed inquiry.

## Acceptance checks

Intended quality is an understandable, correctable decision with visible dependencies and legitimate refusal. R1–R5 define proposed behavioral checks. No check has been run and there is no observed implementation behavior.

Before interaction testing, technical verification must inspect keyboard order and focus, responsive reflow, concealment of every task-bearing component, stale summaries, cancellation, clearing while covered or stopped, and absence of network calls, persistent storage and telemetry. Demonstrating those behaviors would establish only the tested technical behavior.

Human review must separately examine whether the task is wanted, route labels imply provision, explanations impose excessive reading, privacy controls are discoverable and refusal feels legitimate. Patron, librarian and accessibility-practitioner review remains pending. Learning, transfer and flourishing require separate evidence and cannot be inferred from a changed plan, speed or completion.

## Evidence and unknowns

Evidence references are sequence 2's preserved context and sequence 5's domain draft. Neither supplies participant observations, approved requirements, technical results or field success. Historical sequence labels embedded in the parent are background and are not additional event citations here.

What changes after the proposed hypothetical challenge: staff preference persists while availability becomes unresolved; dependent descriptions update; reconsideration never substitutes a route automatically. The before/after proposal also requires bounded snapshots and complete clearing of both. These refine the current Design; they do not invalidate the earlier Map dependency account or require rerunning it.

Unknowns include demand for the tool, real event routes, account necessity, paper acceptance, staffing windows, language arrangements, device behavior and acceptable facilitation workload. Rival explanations for difficulty include service friction, unclear wording, inaccessible interaction and interrupted device time. Apparent ease could reflect familiarity or facilitator prompting. Field evidence remains pending.

## Next decision

Carry these draft state rules into a reviewable screen outline and matching paper packet. Have accountable patron, librarian and accessibility-practitioner review determine whether the task and support burden are appropriate, retaining dissent and proposed corrections. A later Build may implement a candidate for technical and interaction testing; no approval, pilot authorization or efficacy is supplied by this contribution.

response.challenged_assumption: A before/after plan remains faithful and private without explicit snapshot rules, and selecting assistance can be treated as an available next step.
response.decision: Refine the current Design with explicit dependency, comparison, cancellation and recovery rules; prepare paired screen and paper materials for pending human review.
drawbacks: Before/after comparison adds state and reading burden.
Fixed choices may omit an acceptable action.
Paper preparation and oral facilitation require capacity that is currently unknown.
flourishing: Agency and dignity require correction and refusal without justification or deficit labels.
Access and belonging depend on usable routes, language arrangements and acceptable support.
Sustainable workload, learning and transfer need separate reviewed evidence; completion establishes none of them.
human_capabilities: Patrons control route choice, correction, passing, pause and refusal through selection, pointing or speech.
Librarians and service owners must establish actual route conditions, assistance boundaries and feasible workload.
Patrons and accessibility practitioners must review comprehension, recovery, language access and shared-device handling.
response.message: Sequence 2 preserves parent context; it reports no executed check or human approval. Sequence 5 strengthens the fictional event journey and separates route preference from provision. My Systems challenge is that a correctable before/after plan introduces additional state that can become stale, survive clearing or imply that requested help exists. The Design needs explicit dependency and recovery rules. The requirements below are expert draft proposals for review; field evidence remains pending.
objections: Clearer notices or removal of an unnecessary account requirement may address the problem more directly.
Patrons may find the simulation burdensome or reject every offered route.
A library may lack capacity for facilitation, printing or reviewed language versions.
risks: A selected support request could be displayed as available assistance.
Correction or clearing could leave an earlier plan in feedback, hidden content or optional practice.
Service barriers could be misread as patron deficits or evidence of a training need.
system_capabilities: Represent explicit choices separately from authored conditions and unknown real provision.
Derive a correctable initial/current plan without personal fields, scores or inferred capability.
Keep visibility, activity and content presence independent; clear every candidate-held task snapshot.
tradeoffs: Keep a useful initial/current comparison while retaining only those two temporary snapshots.
Reveal dependencies near relevant choices while keeping detailed review information in Help.
Offer supported practice without making facilitation or a finished plan necessary.

The proposed task is to explore an invented community event, inspect an authored participation requirement and choose an acceptable next step. The people whose interests require review are adult patrons with varied reading, language and device access; librarians and volunteers who may provide assistance; and service owners who control actual event routes. None participate in this demonstration.

D1.problem challenge: difficulty with an account step may reflect an avoidable service requirement, unclear notice or unavailable route. The product must not treat independent online progress as the problem to solve. D5.context challenge: choosing help does not create staff capacity, language assistance, connectivity or time on a shared computer.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: patrons control whether to continue and may respond by selecting, pointing or speaking. Passing and declining require no justification. Librarians define what assistance can reasonably cover; service owners verify real routes before any later service use. Patron and practitioner review must examine whether the proposed task is wanted and understandable.

System requirements: keep preference separate from provision. Choosing staff help changes the draft support request, not the staff availability state. Choosing paper opens complete invented materials, not a claim that the real service accepts paper.

Authority remains external to the candidate: it cannot register, reserve help, establish eligibility, verify accounts or determine capability. The candidate should use no open-text fields for this task; fixed choices can express its core decisions without inviting personal information.

## Experience and decisions

Invented notice: “Community Drawing Hour offers a morning session and an afternoon session. Materials are provided in this example. The notice says: ‘Confirm your place.’ The route details below are invented for practice.” Session preference is optional and is not a booking.

Offer a local mock online route, asking staff to explain a step, a complete paper practice route, and pause/decline. Include “No route works for me” and “Leave undecided.” Reveal route details when selected. The online detail says: “This example portal requires an account step before confirmation. The changed-condition design makes service dependency visible, but may add reading burden. Keep its initial wording short and reveal explanations on request. A complete paper route adds preparation and handling work, but provides a concrete non-AI comparison.

Retain the objection that clearer notices could solve the underlying problem more directly. Alternatives include the paper packet, conversation with available staff and revising service information before building a tool. Reviewers may prefer an alternative or reject the candidate.

Card B — Routes and conditions. “Online practice: the invented portal includes an account step; do not supply account information. Card C — Before plan. “Route: online / staff explanation / paper practice / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect the requirement / seek an explanation if support exists / examine another route / pause / stop / undecided. Support wanted: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none chosen. Card D — Changed condition. “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Keep your preference, change it, leave it unresolved or stop. Waiting has no promised duration. No route becomes available merely because you choose it.”

## Acceptance checks

Intended quality: an understandable, correctable route decision that preserves patron control and exposes service dependencies. Proposed checks in R1–R6 cover interaction behavior, privacy, language uncertainty and equivalent alternatives. None has been executed.

Technical verification must separately inspect keyboard order, visible focus, reflow, concealment, stale summaries, confirmed clearing and absence of network, storage and telemetry. Human interaction review must examine whether labels imply real provision, whether stopping is socially acceptable, and what assistance or reading burden the journey creates.

Review flourishing without equating task completion with success: agency includes refusal; dignity excludes deficit labels; access depends on actual conditions; belonging includes usable language arrangements; sustainable workload includes facilitation demand. Learning and transfer require separately reviewed evidence from a different task with support conditions documented.

It is a preservation event, not a new interaction finding. Sequence 5 supplies the current domain proposal, including the fictional event, separate preference and provision, complete paper materials and optional practice.

The task is to inspect the invented Community Drawing Hour notice, consider its authored confirmation requirement and choose an acceptable next step. Adult patrons, librarians, volunteers, service owners and accessibility practitioners have relevant interests; none participate in this demonstration.

D1.problem challenge: an unfamiliar account step may indicate unnecessary service friction, unclear information, language mismatch or unavailable support. More patron training is only one possible response and has no supporting evidence here. An acceptable outcome includes an unresolved plan, paper practice, seeking an explanation when assistance exists, or stopping.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: patrons retain authority over continuing and correcting their choices. Pointing, speaking, passing and declining remain legitimate. Available facilitators may read an authored notice or restate an explicit selection, but must not infer agreement, supply a preferred answer or promise assistance. Librarians and service owners must establish actual service conditions before any later operational use.

System requirements: distinguish the patron's preference, the fictional condition being explored, real provision that remains unknown, and the draft next action. Selecting staff help records a preference; it cannot create a staffed opportunity. Selecting paper practice opens complete invented materials; it cannot establish real paper acceptance. The mock online route may describe an account requirement but must contain no account or credential controls.

The coupling is conditional: a desired action may depend on understandable information, a usable route, device time and suitable assistance. The candidate can expose those dependencies and support reconsideration. It cannot supply missing service capacity. Authority over the event requirement belongs to the service owner; authority over offered assistance belongs to its provider; the patron controls participation in this exercise.

## Experience and decisions

Keep the primary journey short: explore the invented notice, choose a route, inspect one condition and review a draft. Use the four text-labelled route choices proposed in the seed: mock online practice, staff explanation, complete paper practice, and pause/decline. Also permit no workable route and undecided without requiring an explanation. Use fixed controls and no open-text fields for this candidate.

The first review describes the current choice. An optional explicit action, “Keep this as my initial plan,” records a temporary comparison snapshot. Without that action, show “Initial plan not recorded”; do not fabricate a baseline. Invite the authored change, “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit.” Keep the patron's preference and display its unresolved dependency. Offer reconsideration, waiting without a promised duration, remaining undecided or stopping. Never select another route automatically.

The current plan describes route, next action, control boundary, requested support and fallback. It always states “Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.” Changed fields receive descriptive feedback, such as “You changed from staff explanation to paper practice. Real paper acceptance is unknown.” Feedback must derive from explicit choices rather than judge progress.

The optional Neighborhood Story Circle task uses fewer suggestions and its own authored notice. Entering it requires a clear choice to replace the current task, with an opportunity to cancel. It unlocks nothing. Any apparent independence remains uninterpreted until reviewed evidence documents prior familiarity and support.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Dependency honesty. Origin: Systems engineer, D1.coupling; domain specialist at sequence 5; preserved Map dependency separation in sequence 2. Selecting a route must reveal its authored requirement, the party controlling it, real provision marked unknown and an action the patron can choose. Selecting staff explanation must leave staff availability unchanged. Acceptance check: select staff explanation, apply fictional unavailability and inspect the plan; the preference remains visible, the dependency becomes unresolved, no help is confirmed and every other route or refusal remains selectable. Context boundary: the changed condition is hypothetical and actual staffing is unknown.

R2 — Correctable comparison. Origin: Systems engineer, D4.verification; before/after proposal at sequence 5; sequence 2's temporary-memory and correction boundaries. Retain at most an explicitly recorded initial snapshot and the current draft within the active session. Generate descriptions from those selections; do not maintain an accumulating choice log. “Correct initial plan” must be distinct from “Change current plan,” with plain labels explaining which side changes. Acceptance check: record an initial staff preference, change the current route to paper, then correct the initial route to undecided. The comparison must describe those exact states and remove obsolete staff-derived claims. A cleared snapshot must never be reconstructed. Context boundary: before/after comparison is a design intention, not measured reflection or learning.

R3 — Separate privacy, activity and content. Origin: Systems engineer, D1.coupling and D4.verification; domain privacy requirement at sequence 5; preserved focus and concealment requirements in sequence 2. Place Cover, Clear and Stop before task controls in keyboard order. Cover hides every choice-bearing view, including both snapshots, feedback, optional practice and assistance descriptions, from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access. Focus moves to a neutral status. Reveal changes visibility only. Resume is an explicit separate action when activity is paused. Clear remains available while covered or stopped and removes all candidate-held selections and derived task content before confirming its limited scope. It preserves pause or stop and does not create a new draft. Acceptance check: exercise these transitions from an initial/current comparison, a changed-condition view and optional practice; verify neutral focus, no exposed choices while covered, no stale descriptions after clearing and no automatic restart. Context boundary: clearing the candidate does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.

R4 — Recovery without inferred intent. Origin: Systems engineer, D4.verification; sequence 2's interruption and loss boundaries; sequence 5's meaningful refusal. A fictional interruption pauses activity without changing route preference. Cancel closes a pending route change, task replacement or clear confirmation without modifying choices. If the page is reloaded, temporary task state is lost: the opening explains that no prior draft is restored and offers a fresh undecided task, paper materials or stopping. Acceptance check: cancel each pending action, interrupt a changed plan, then reload; unchanged choices survive cancellation, interruption does not silently resume, and reload restores no selections. Context boundary: no persistent storage or recovery history is permitted; these checks have not been executed.

R5 — Equivalent non-AI task and feasible support. Origin: Systems engineer, D1.problem and D1.coupling; domain packet at sequence 5; paper comparison and workload concerns preserved in sequence 2. Make the complete paper packet available before any digital choice. The packet must carry the same authored requirement, changed condition, initial/current choices, control boundary, correction and refusal. Oral assistance is conditional on an actually available person. Acceptance check: a reviewer can conduct the fictional decision using only the packet, without opening the digital route or supplying personal information; the facilitator can restate a corrected choice without selecting an answer. Context boundary: printing, physical access, language arrangements and handling effort need practitioner and affected-person review.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

The initial/current comparison makes a changed decision inspectable but adds state and wording. Keep it optional, retain only two temporary snapshots and show expanded explanations on request. Correctability matters more than filling every field.

Preserve dissent that a planning tool may be unnecessary. A clearer notice, verified route information or removal of a needless account step could address the barrier at its source. Complete paper practice and an ordinary conversation with available staff are non-AI options. None establishes operational service access.

Complete invented paper/facilitation packet for this state design:

Card A — Mission and notice. “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon sessions and says ‘Confirm your place.’ Choose a possible next step; you are not registering. Point, speak, mark, pass, pause or stop. Use no personal information.”

Card B — Route conditions. “Online practice: inspect an invented account requirement; do not create an account or supply details. Staff explanation: ask someone to explain a step if suitable assistance exists; real availability and language support are unknown. Paper practice: use these cards; real acceptance of paper is unknown. No workable route and undecided are valid choices.”

Card C — Initial plan, optional. “Route: online practice / staff explanation / paper practice / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect requirement / seek explanation if assistance exists / examine another route / wait without a promised time / pause / stop / undecided. Support wanted: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: examine another route / remain undecided / pause / stop.” Record only if wanted. No written reason is required.

Card D — Changed condition. “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Your preference does not make assistance available. Keep it unresolved, reconsider a route, wait without a promised duration, pause or stop.”

Card E — Current plan and correction. Repeat Card C's choices for the current plan. “The service owner controls the requirement; assistance providers control what help they offer; you control continuing. Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.” Correct the initial or current selection explicitly, or leave either blank. The facilitator restates the selected side and accepts correction without asking for justification.

Card F — Handling and facilitation. “Covering or folding cards conceals them; it does not erase them. Before marking, agree how cards will be handled. Stop or pass without explanation.” Facilitator script: “Would you like to point, speak, mark, pass or stop? Shall I read the notice? Which route, if any? Here is the imagined change. Keep or change your choice? Which plan should I correct?” Do not record personal information, infer understanding or promise service support.

Optional practice card — “Neighborhood Story Circle is invented. Its notice says ‘Check joining arrangements.’ Use Cards B, C and E to choose a next step. Imagine shared-computer time ends. Keep, revise, pause or stop.” Offer extra prompts only if requested; document their use in any later reviewed inquiry.

## Acceptance checks

Intended quality is an understandable, correctable decision with visible dependencies and legitimate refusal. R1–R5 define proposed behavioral checks. No check has been run and there is no observed implementation behavior.

Before interaction testing, technical verification must inspect keyboard order and focus, responsive reflow, concealment of every task-bearing component, stale summaries, cancellation, clearing while covered or stopped, and absence of network calls, persistent storage and telemetry. Demonstrating those behaviors would establish only the tested technical behavior.

Human review must separately examine whether the task is wanted, route labels imply provision, explanations impose excessive reading, privacy controls are discoverable and refusal feels legitimate. Patron, librarian and accessibility-practitioner review remains pending. Learning, transfer and flourishing require separate evidence and cannot be inferred from a changed plan, speed or completion.

## Evidence and unknowns

Evidence references are sequence 2's preserved context and sequence 5's domain draft. Neither supplies participant observations, approved requirements, technical results or field success. Historical sequence labels embedded in the parent are background and are not additional event citations here.

What changes after the proposed hypothetical challenge: staff preference persists while availability becomes unresolved; dependent descriptions update; reconsideration never substitutes a route automatically. The before/after proposal also requires bounded snapshots and complete clearing of both. These refine the current Design; they do not invalidate the earlier Map dependency account or require rerunning it.

Unknowns include demand for the tool, real event routes, account necessity, paper acceptance, staffing windows, language arrangements, device behavior and acceptable facilitation workload. Rival explanations for difficulty include service friction, unclear wording, inaccessible interaction and interrupted device time. Apparent ease could reflect familiarity or facilitator prompting. Field evidence remains pending.

Carry these draft state rules into a reviewable screen outline and matching paper packet. Provisional integrated Design revision for public deliberation in a rehearsal. Sequence 24 integrates the dependency model and retention boundaries; sequence 20 separates supported planning from optional practice and learning inquiry. REVISION AND SCOPE
Revise Design once: replace nominal reachability with explicit placement, reflow and focus requirements. The dependency model and problem frame remain applicable; the earliest artifact needing this change is Design. The unresolved Understand human-review gate remains pending, without requesting another revision of Understand.

SCREEN ORDER AND ACCESS
Place a short strip labeled “Privacy and stopping” before planning content and first among interactive controls in keyboard order. Use neutral buttons: “Conceal draft,” “Clear draft,” and “Stop exercise.” Keep applicable actions accessible during active, paused, stopped and concealed states; clearing must remain available without revealing content.
The layout must wrap controls without horizontal scrolling, clipping or overlap at magnification settings selected through human review. Any persistent positioning must not obscure controls, focused elements or task content. Review must examine discoverability from within the planning area, not merely from the initial screen. Do not rely on assumed shortcuts, devices or staff intervention. These are requirements to verify, not accessibility claims.

FICTIONAL PLANNING CONTENT
Opening: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Its notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Real routes and assistance availability are unknown. Use fictional choices only.”
Approach choices: consider online; check for paper; check for staffed help; availability unknown; none works; undecided. Next-action choices: examine the notice; ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available; check another route; my action is not listed; undecided. Both default to undecided. No explanation is required for a missing action.
“Describe my draft” optionally presents fixed text describing current selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” Visible descriptions update immediately after correction. No preferred route, praise, score or completion judgment is allowed.

PRIVACY AND FOCUS TRANSITIONS
Conceal hides selectors, descriptions and all choice-specific messages, including interruption output, from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access. Move focus to a neutral status: “Fictional content remains in this session.” Provide explicit reveal, clear and stop controls. Reveal restores visibility only; it must not resume activity automatically or announce a choice-specific summary.
Clear removes candidate-held choices, descriptions and choice-specific messages. Move focus to: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Preserve paused or stopped activity. Do not recreate a draft automatically. A new undecided draft requires explicit action; resuming also requires explicit action. Focus destinations must remain available and understandable without exposing choices.
Use temporary current-draft memory only: no free text, history, analytics, persistent storage, exports, transmissions or automatic staff requests. All implementation boundaries require verification.

OPTIONAL CHANGE AND RECOVERY
Offer separate invitations to try a confusing notice or rehearse an interruption. Neither unlocks assistance or finishing. Confusion repeats that confirmation and help availability remain unresolved. Interruption states: “Imagine the shared-computer session ends before you continue,” and pauses activity. Offer keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; privacy controls remain available. No automatic recovery or inferred intention is permitted. If draft loss is known, disclose it and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices.

Prepare a paper card with the same notice, approach and action choices, correction, uncertainty, pause and stop. Pointing or speaking is sufficient; writing is optional and fictional only. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it; discreet handling needs review. Ordinary conversation with available staff and clearer service notices remain alternatives. Staff capacity is unknown; reviewers may prefer an alternative or reject the tool.

REVIEW AND NEXT ACTION
Prepare this revised screen outline, paper card and fictional transition checks. Proposed checks cover keyboard discovery during interruption, magnified reflow, neutral focus, complete concealment, stale descriptions, clear while stopped, and storage/transmission boundaries. None has been performed.
Accountable patron and librarian review must examine framing, access, privacy, missing actions and workload before approved design. Separate any voluntary learning inquiry using another fictional task and documented support conditions; completion, speed or one revised plan cannot establish retention or transfer.","content_hash":"3f234e938602b268ec8f69c3c64e17b5fad30fe53fda30a65729cd72ee6aa306","revision":2},"model":{"body":"STATUS AND BASIS
