## Human and system capability

Human requirements: patrons retain authority over whether to participate, what help they want and which explanation represents their choice. Selecting, pointing or speaking may express a choice; silence must not be interpreted as agreement. Passing requires no reason. An actually available facilitator may read authored information or restate selections, but must accept correction and avoid steering toward a preferred route.

System requirements: present the mission and route choices with text alternatives, keep fictional conditions distinct from unknown real provision, and reveal detail without forcing additional decisions. Origin: Learning scientist, D4.transfer; optional second situation at sequences 5, 7 and 9, and the parent learning boundary preserved at sequence 2. Label Story Circle as optional practice, not a transfer test. Give it its own notice and device-time condition; offer help on request without penalty. Acceptance check: enter practice, request detail, leave joining arrangements unresolved, revise or stop. No reward, independence label, competence claim or unlocked service appears. The second task must not invent an account requirement. Context: similar route controls and immediate timing may allow interface familiarity to explain performance.

L4 — Keep any later retention inquiry separate. Origin: Learning scientist, D4.transfer; sequence 2 preserves the requirement for a different task and documented support conditions. The candidate must not retain a learning history, schedule follow-up or infer retention from the initial/current comparison. If humans later authorize an inquiry, use a different fictional notice after a review-selected interval and document the conditions of performance: available information, requested and supplied assistance, prior familiarity and interruptions. Acceptance check for this candidate: every output and Help statement distinguishes immediate supported practice from untested later retention and adaptation. Any future inquiry protocol must be reviewed before use; no interval, recruitment or authorization is established here.

L5 — Preserve a complete non-AI practice route. Origin: Learning scientist, D2.practice and D4.transfer; complete packets at sequences 5, 7 and 9. Keep the same notice, condition, choices, correction and refusal available on paper before digital participation. Pointing or speaking is sufficient if an appropriate person is actually available. Acceptance check: a reviewer can conduct the fictional decision using only the packet below, without digital instructions, personal details or a supplied preferred answer. Printing, language access, handling and facilitator workload remain unknown.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Descriptive feedback can support reconsideration but also supply reasoning the patron has not independently produced. Keep wording tied to explicit selections and do not treat accepting the summary as understanding. Fewer suggestions may expose a different support need, but may also increase reading and memory demands; Help must remain available.

Retain dissent that a learning exercise may be unnecessary. Improving the event notice, verifying route information or removing a needless account step could address the service barrier directly. Ordinary conversation with available staff and the following paper packet are non-AI alternatives. Review may favor an alternative or stopping development.

Complete invented paper practice packet:

Card A — Mission and notice. “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Its notice offers morning or afternoon sessions and says ‘Confirm your place.’ Choose a possible next step; this does not register anyone. Use no personal information. Point, speak, mark, pass, pause or stop.”

Card B — Routes and conditions. “Online practice: inspect an invented account requirement; create no account and provide no details. Staff explanation: seek an explanation if suitable assistance exists; real availability and language support are unknown. Paper practice: use these cards; real paper acceptance is unknown. No workable route and undecided are legitimate choices.”

Card C — Optional initial plan. “Route: online / staff explanation / paper practice / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect requirement / seek explanation if support exists / examine another route / wait without a promised time / action not listed / undecided / pause / stop. Support preference: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: another route / undecided / pause / stop.” Leave any item blank. No reason is required.

Card D — Changed condition. “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Keep your preference unresolved, change route, wait without a promised duration, leave undecided, pause or stop. Selecting help does not make it available.”

Card E — Current plan and correction. Repeat Card C for the current plan. “You control continuing. The service owner controls the requirement. Assistance providers control support offered. Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.” Correct either plan by replacing a mark or requesting a restatement. An unrecorded initial plan remains unrecorded. No answer is scored.

Card F — Optional practice and facilitation. “Neighborhood Story Circle is invented. Its notice says ‘Check joining arrangements.’ Those arrangements are unresolved. Choose a possible route and next action using Card C. Imagine shared-computer time ends. Keep, change, pause or stop; review using Card E.” Facilitator script: “Would you like the notice read aloud? Which route, if any? Would you like more detail? Keep or change your choice? Shall I restate it so you can correct it?” Ask permission, accept passing and supply no preferred answer. Before marking cards, agree how they will be handled. Covering conceals paper but does not erase it. This practice establishes no learning or transfer.

## Acceptance checks

L1–L5 are proposed checks, not completed tests. Intended quality is a voluntary, inspectable and correctable decision with clear support boundaries. Technical verification may establish that descriptions match selections, corrections remove stale content and optional practice preserves help. It cannot establish comprehension or learning.

Pending human interaction review must examine whether people can recognize what remains unresolved, whether feedback represents their choice, and whether assistance or reading burden is acceptable. Refusal is valid participation, not a failed task. Preserve contrary interpretations and requested corrections.

Learning, retention and transfer require separate reviewed task evidence. Completion, speed, a changed plan, fewer clicks or fewer prompts are insufficient. Agency, dignity, access, belonging and sustainable workload also require evidence about actual participation conditions; none has been observed.

## Evidence and unknowns

Actual earlier references are sequence 2's preserved context and the drafts at sequences 5, 7 and 9. Embedded historical labels in sequence 2 are not additional event evidence. No human approval or field result is supplied.

After the hypothetical unavailable-staff challenge, feedback must expose the unresolved assistance dependency while preserving patron preference. This contribution adds a learning boundary: revising that preference is inspectable behavior, not evidence of improved capability. Story Circle also retains unknown joining arrangements rather than inheriting the account condition from Drawing Hour.

Rival explanations for apparent ease include prior service familiarity, visible suggestions, repeated controls and facilitator prompting. Difficulty could reflect ambiguous wording, language mismatch, inaccessible controls, interrupted device time or unavailable assistance. Unknowns include whether the exercise is wanted, whether its representations are understood, what support is sustainable, and whether any later adaptation occurs. Field evidence remains pending.

## Next decision

Refine the current Design with L1–L5 and prepare the screen outline and paper packet for pending patron, librarian and practitioner review. Examine the value and burden of practice before planning a learning inquiry. Retain dissent, correction and the possibility of a non-AI service improvement. A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Maintain independent fields:

Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability.

response.artifact_body:
## Problem and people

Responsible AI specialist expert draft for Design deliberation in a rehearsal. Nothing here is an approved requirement, participant observation or executed check. Sequence 2 preserves parent Understand, Map and Design context; its embedded historical labels are not additional evidence references. Sequences 5, 7, 9 and 11 are current specialist proposals.

Access Studio invites an adult patron to explore the invented Community Drawing Hour, inspect an authored account requirement and choose a possible next step. Adult patrons, librarians, volunteers, service owners and accessibility practitioners have relevant interests; none participate in this demonstration.

The delegation challenge is that readable synthesis can acquire authority beyond its source choices. A plan saying someone will ask staff can be mistaken for a feasible action, a sent request or an endorsed route. The privacy challenge is that fictional route and support preferences still reveal the exercise participant's selections to nearby people. Absence of personal fields does not by itself establish a discreet handoff.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: the patron decides whether to participate and whether the displayed description represents their choice. Selecting, pointing or speaking are possible ways to express a decision; silence is not agreement. A facilitator must ask permission to read or restate, accept correction and avoid choosing an answer. Suitable assistance must actually exist before oral facilitation can occur.

Service owners control actual event requirements and accepted routes. Assistance providers control the support they offer. Librarians must examine shared-device arrangements, printing and facilitation burden. Patron and practitioner review must examine comprehension, discoverability, privacy and whether the exercise is wanted. These human gates remain unmet.

System requirements: the candidate may display authored information and describe explicit selections. It may not register, contact staff, verify an account, determine eligibility, recommend a consequential route, infer consent or judge capability. Requested support, authored example availability and unknown real provision must remain separate. The task needs no model inference; fixed local rules can generate its descriptive output.

## Experience and decisions

The route board offers mock online practice, staff explanation, complete paper practice and pause or decline. No workable route, undecided and an unlisted next action remain equally legitimate. No personal, account or credential fields are needed.

Each route reveals its consequence and authority boundary beside the choice. Online practice describes the invented account step without creating an account. Staff explanation records a preference and says real assistance and language support are unknown; no request is sent. Paper practice opens complete invented materials and says real paper acceptance is unknown.

Use conditional output: "Your draft seeks an explanation if suitable assistance exists." Avoid "Staff will help you." The review states "Fictional plan; no registration or request sent" next to the generated description. An unset support choice remains "None selected," never "No support needed." Agreeing that text matches a choice establishes only that representation, not comprehension, consent to a service or demonstrated proficiency.

The initial snapshot is optional. Correcting it changes the initial representation; changing the current plan changes the current representation. Cancellation leaves both untouched. Do not retain an additional history of revisions. Unlisted or rejected wording yields an unresolved description without asking for an explanation.

Applying the hypothetical unavailable-staff condition preserves the patron's preference and exposes its unresolved dependency. It offers reconsideration, waiting without a promised duration, remaining undecided, pausing or stopping. It must not silently select paper or online practice. Optional Story Circle practice uses its own notice and device-time condition, with joining arrangements unresolved rather than an inherited account requirement.

## Requirements and rationale

RA1 — Delegation boundary. Origin: Responsible AI specialist, D3.delegation; preference/provision proposals at sequences 5 and 7 and local authority wording at sequence 9. Place the controlling party, fictional condition and unknown real provision beside each route consequence and in the review. Human reason: a patron must be able to distinguish their choice from another party's commitment. System reason: descriptive text must not manufacture provision or authority. Acceptance check: select staff explanation and apply fictional unavailability; the preference persists, assistance remains unresolved, no request is confirmed and no alternative is selected automatically. Context: staffing is unknown and the change is authored, not an observed incident.

RA2 — Accountable representation. Origin: Responsible AI specialist, D3.delegation; correction at sequence 7, voluntary participation at sequence 9 and descriptive feedback at sequence 11. Give distinct controls for correcting the initial plan, changing the current plan and rejecting an unlisted action without free text. Replace dependent descriptions and remove obsolete feedback after correction. Human reason: fluent wording must remain contestable. System reason: every claim must be attributable to explicit selections and stated conditions. Acceptance check: record initial staff preference, change current preference to paper, correct initial preference to undecided and cancel another edit. Both views must reflect those exact choices; no obsolete staff claim, score or assertion of understanding may remain. Comprehension of the comparison is untested.

RA3 — Bounded retention without surveillance. Origin: Responsible AI specialist, D5.privacy; temporary-memory boundary preserved at sequence 2 and bounded snapshots at sequence 7. Keep at most the optional initial snapshot, current draft and state necessary for the active interaction. Do not add a chronological choice log, identifiers, timestamps of patron actions, support-use analytics, exports or inference about independence. Human reason: practice must not become monitoring of patron behavior. System reason: unnecessary retained state increases exposure and clearing complexity. Acceptance check: inspect the implementation for network, telemetry, persistent storage and accumulated action history; inspect reload behavior for absence of restored selections. These checks are pending. A route choice is neither permission to disclose nor evidence of an ability need.

RA4 — Shared-device cover and handoff. Origin: Responsible AI specialist, D5.privacy; complete concealment preserved at sequence 2 and privacy/activity/content separation at sequences 7 and 9. Put Cover, Clear and Stop before task controls in keyboard order. Cover removes all choice-bearing content from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access, including initial/current plans, feedback, pending edits and any displayed paper selections. Focus moves to neutral status. Reveal restores visibility only; resumption remains explicit. Confirmed Clear removes candidate-held choices, snapshots, pending edits and derived messages, then presents a neutral confirmation of that limited scope. It preserves paused or stopped activity and does not create a fresh draft. Cancellation preserves content. Human reason: an interruption must leave usable control over exposure and handoff. System reason: hiding one panel cannot conceal every representation. Acceptance check: exercise these actions from comparison, changed-condition and optional-practice states, including clearing while covered; inspect focus, live announcements and stale content. Covering is concealment, not erasure. No device-wide deletion claim is permitted.

RA5 — Human gates and non-AI equivalence. Origin: Responsible AI specialist, D3.delegation and D5.privacy; human gates preserved at sequence 2, paper route at sequence 5, participation boundaries at sequence 9 and learning limits at sequence 11. Make the complete packet below available before digital participation. No finished plan, explanation or second task is required. Human reason: refusal and alternatives must be usable rather than ceremonial. System reason: a candidate cannot approve its own service fit or privacy adequacy. Acceptance check: a reviewer can conduct the fictional task using only the packet, correct either plan and stop without personal details or a preferred answer. Patron, librarian and practitioner review must separately examine wantedness, language arrangements, handling and workload. Any later pilot requires accountable human review and interaction testing; this draft supplies neither authorization nor approval.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

The optional comparison can make reconsideration visible but retains additional choice-bearing content and adds memory demands. Review may remove it while preserving a correctable current plan. Fixed choices reduce personal disclosure but may omit a desired action; unlisted and undecided outcomes must remain valid.

Retain dissent that improving the notice or removing needless service friction could address the underlying problem more directly. A static authored route board, the paper packet and conversation with actually available staff are non-AI alternatives. None establishes operational access. Reviewers may prefer an alternative or stop development.

Complete invented paper/facilitation packet:

Card A — Mission and notice. "Community Drawing Hour is fictional. Its notice offers morning or afternoon sessions and says ‘Confirm your place.’ Explore a possible next step; this does not register anyone. Use no personal information. Point, speak, mark, pass, pause or stop. Session preference is optional."

Card B — Routes and conditions. "Online practice: inspect an invented account requirement; create no account and provide no details. Staff explanation: seek an explanation if suitable assistance exists; real availability and language support are unknown. Paper practice: use these cards; real service acceptance of paper is unknown. No workable route and undecided are legitimate choices."

Card C — Optional initial plan. "Route: online practice / staff explanation / paper practice / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect requirement / seek explanation if assistance exists / examine another route / wait without a promised duration / action not listed / undecided / pause / stop. Support preference: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: examine another route / remain undecided / pause / stop." Leave any item blank. No reason is required. None selected does not establish that support is unnecessary.

Card D — Changed condition. "Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Keep your preference unresolved, change route, wait without a promised duration, leave undecided, pause or stop. Choosing assistance does not make it available."

Card E — Current plan and correction. Repeat Card C's choices for the current plan. "You control continuing. The service owner controls the requirement. Assistance providers control offered support. Fictional plan; no registration or request sent." Identify whether a correction changes the initial or current plan. Replace a mark or request a restatement. An unrecorded initial plan stays unrecorded; no answer is scored.

Card F — Handling and facilitation. "Before marking, agree who may see the cards and how they will be handled afterward. Leave them unmarked if preferred. Folding or covering conceals them; it does not erase them." Facilitator script: "Would you like to point, speak, mark, pass or stop? May I read the notice? Which route, if any? Would you like the imagined change? May I restate your selection so you can correct it?" Wait for an explicit response; collect no personal details, promise no service assistance and infer no understanding. Facilitation depends on an actually available person.

Optional practice card — "Neighborhood Story Circle is fictional. Its notice says ‘Check joining arrangements’; those arrangements remain unresolved. Use Card C to choose a possible route and next action. Imagine shared-computer time ends. Keep, revise, pause or stop; review with Card E. More explanation is available on request if an appropriate facilitator exists. This practice establishes no learning or transfer."

## Acceptance checks

RA1–RA5 describe proposed observable checks. Intended quality is an understandable, voluntary and correctable decision with honest authority boundaries and usable privacy controls. No technical behavior has been observed and no check has been executed.

Technical verification must inspect all reachable privacy and correction states, keyboard focus, reflow, announcements, stale content and absence of network, storage, telemetry, personal fields and external navigation. Passing those checks would establish only the tested behavior, not privacy in every device environment or accessibility certification.

Affected-person and practitioner review must separately examine whether wording implies provision, whether a patron can reject a summary, whether refusal feels legitimate and whether concealment and clearing are discoverable during interruption. Learning, transfer, agency, dignity, access, belonging and sustainable workload remain untested. Completion, speed or fewer prompts cannot establish those outcomes.

## Evidence and unknowns

Sequence 2 is the supplied preservation event, not a privacy incident or newly verified finding. Sequences 5, 7, 9 and 11 provide draft proposals. They contain no participant observations, human approval or field results. Field evidence remains pending.

After the hypothetical unavailable-staff challenge, the requirement changes from presenting help as an ordinary next step to preserving a preference with an unresolved provision dependency. This contribution additionally constrains the authority of generated wording and the exposure of snapshots, pending edits and feedback during handoff. These refine current Design; no earlier artifact revision is requested.

Rival explanations for difficulty include ambiguous notices, language mismatch, inaccessible controls, interrupted device time and unavailable assistance. Apparent ease could reflect prior familiarity, visible suggestions or facilitator steering. Unknowns include whether the exercise is wanted, actual routes, account necessity, paper acceptance, staffing, language arrangements, shared-device behavior and acceptable support workload.

R2 — Correctable comparison. Origin: Systems engineer, D4.verification; before/after proposal at sequence 5; sequence 2's temporary-memory and correction boundaries. Retain at most an explicitly recorded initial snapshot and the current draft within the active session. Generate descriptions from those selections; do not maintain an accumulating choice log. “Correct initial plan” must be distinct from “Change current plan,” with plain labels explaining which side changes. Acceptance check: record an initial staff preference, change the current route to paper, then correct the initial route to undecided. The comparison must describe those exact states and remove obsolete staff-derived claims. A cleared snapshot must never be reconstructed. Context boundary: before/after comparison is a design intention, not measured reflection or learning.

Origin: Systems engineer, D1.coupling and D4.verification; domain privacy requirement at sequence 5; preserved focus and concealment requirements in sequence 2. Place Cover, Clear and Stop before task controls in keyboard order. Cover hides every choice-bearing view, including both snapshots, feedback, optional practice and assistance descriptions, from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access. Focus moves to a neutral status. Reveal changes visibility only. Resume is an explicit separate action when activity is paused. Clear remains available while covered or stopped and removes all candidate-held selections and derived task content before confirming its limited scope. It preserves pause or stop and does not create a new draft. Acceptance check: exercise these transitions from an initial/current comparison, a changed-condition view and optional practice; verify neutral focus, no exposed choices while covered, no stale descriptions after clearing and no automatic restart. Context boundary: clearing the candidate does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.

A fictional interruption pauses activity without changing route preference. Cancel closes a pending route change, task replacement or clear confirmation without modifying choices. If the page is reloaded, temporary task state is lost: the opening explains that no prior draft is restored and offers a fresh undecided task, paper materials or stopping. Acceptance check: cancel each pending action, interrupt a changed plan, then reload; unchanged choices survive cancellation, interruption does not silently resume, and reload restores no selections. Make the complete paper packet available before any digital choice. The packet must carry the same authored requirement, changed condition, initial/current choices, control boundary, correction and refusal. Oral assistance is conditional on an actually available person. Acceptance check: a reviewer can conduct the fictional decision using only the packet, without opening the digital route or supplying personal information; the facilitator can restate a corrected choice without selecting an answer. Context boundary: printing, physical access, language arrangements and handling effort need practitioner and affected-person review.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

The initial/current comparison makes a changed decision inspectable but adds state and wording. Keep it optional, retain only two temporary snapshots and show expanded explanations on request. Correctability matters more than filling every field.

Preserve dissent that a planning tool may be unnecessary. A clearer notice, verified route information or removal of a needless account step could address the barrier at its source. Complete paper practice and an ordinary conversation with available staff are non-AI options. None establishes operational service access.

## Acceptance checks

Intended quality is an understandable, correctable decision with visible dependencies and legitimate refusal. R1–R5 define proposed behavioral checks. No check has been run and there is no observed implementation behavior.

Before interaction testing, technical verification must inspect keyboard order and focus, responsive reflow, concealment of every task-bearing component, stale summaries, cancellation, clearing while covered or stopped, and absence of network calls, persistent storage and telemetry. Demonstrating those behaviors would establish only the tested technical behavior.

Human review must separately examine whether the task is wanted, route labels imply provision, explanations impose excessive reading, privacy controls are discoverable and refusal feels legitimate. Patron, librarian and accessibility-practitioner review remains pending. Learning, transfer and flourishing require separate evidence and cannot be inferred from a changed plan, speed or completion.

Evidence references are sequence 2's preserved context and sequence 5's domain draft. Neither supplies participant observations, approved requirements, technical results or field success. Historical sequence labels embedded in the parent are background and are not additional event citations here.

The task is to explore the invented Community Drawing Hour, inspect an authored confirmation requirement and choose an acceptable next step. Relevant people include adult patrons with varied reading, language and device access; people providing assistance; and owners of service requirements. Participation may end with a choice, an unresolved condition, paper practice, passing or declining.

The discipline-specific challenge is that offering valid choices does not establish that people can understand, compare or exercise them with acceptable effort. A route board, support selector, initial snapshot, changed condition and final comparison could become a demanding exercise. A complete plan must not become the implied price of participation.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: patrons retain authority over whether to participate, what help they want and which explanation represents their choice. Selecting, pointing or speaking may express a choice; silence must not be interpreted as agreement. Passing requires no reason. An actually available facilitator may read authored information or restate selections, but must accept correction and avoid steering toward a preferred route.

Librarians and service owners must establish real routes, assistance boundaries and feasible support arrangements before operational use. Affected-person and accessibility-practitioner review must determine whether this task is wanted, its wording is understandable and its privacy controls are usable. These human gates remain unmet.

System requirements: present the mission and route choices with text alternatives, keep fictional conditions distinct from unknown real provision, and reveal detail without forcing additional decisions. Generate descriptions only from explicit selections. No personal fields, account controls, scoring, inferred understanding, storage, network activity or automatic service requests are permitted.

A patron controls continuing and changing a preference. Service owners control actual participation requirements. Assistance providers control what support they offer. Choosing help cannot change its availability. These authority boundaries must appear where the dependent decision occurs, not solely in Help.

## Experience and decisions

Opening mission: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Explore its example notice and choose a possible next step. This exercise cannot register anyone. Use fictional choices only.” The notice offers morning and afternoon sessions and says “Confirm your place.” Session preference is optional and must not resemble a reservation.

Use a small illustrated board with text labels: Explore the event, Choose a route, Check a condition, Review your plan. Illustrations provide orientation only. Do not require interaction with an illustration or completion of every step. Paper materials, Help, passing and stopping remain available from the opening.

The route decision offers mock online practice, staff explanation, paper practice and pause or decline, with equally reachable “No route works for me” and “Leave undecided.” No route is preselected. Selecting a route reveals one short consequence and its condition; it does not advance automatically. Longer explanation is available through “More detail,” which can be closed without changing choices or losing focus.

For online practice, show “This invented portal includes an account step. No account is created here.” Controls inspect the requirement, reconsider the route or stop; there are no account or contact fields. Staff explanation records a desired explanation and states that real assistance and language support are unknown. Paper practice opens complete fictional materials and states that real paper acceptance is unknown.

The patron may optionally keep the current selection as an initial plan. Skipping this leaves “Initial plan not recorded.” It does not block the changed condition, current plan or paper route. Support choices are optional and unselected by default; “None selected” does not mean no support is needed.

Offer the authored change: “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit.” Applying it preserves the selected route and marks its assistance dependency unresolved. Show options to keep the preference, reconsider, wait without a promised duration, leave undecided, pause or stop. Do not substitute an online route.

Review shows initial and current route, next action, support preference, control boundary and fallback using short labelled lines. “Fictional plan; no registration or request sent” remains adjacent to the output. “Correct initial plan” and “Change current plan” identify the side being edited. Cancellation preserves both sides. No reason for correction is requested.

Optional Neighborhood Story Circle practice uses fewer suggestions, but retains Help, paper, passing and correction. Choosing it clearly explains that it replaces the current task and offers cancellation. Requesting more support has no penalty and produces no capability label.

R1 — Limit entry burden. Origin: Human-centered designer, D2.prototyping and D5.context; route journey at sequence 5 and bounded comparison at sequence 7. Make the core task one route choice followed by inspection of its consequence. Session, support, initial snapshot and changed-condition practice remain optional. Acceptance check: a reviewer can inspect an online requirement and leave with an undecided next action without completing other selectors; no blocked control, missing-field message or completion judgment appears. R2 — Preserve choice without steering. Origin: Human-centered designer, D3.agency; meaningful refusal at sequences 2 and 5. R3 — Keep dependency information local. Origin: Human-centered designer, D3.agency and D5.context; preference/provision separation at sequences 5 and 7. R4 — Make representation correctable. Origin: Human-centered designer, D2.prototyping and D3.agency; snapshot rules at sequence 7. Progressive detail reduces initial reading but can obscure conditions; therefore essential fiction, availability and control statements remain visible beside decisions. A before/after view makes changes inspectable but adds memory demands; it is optional and may be removed after review. Fixed choices limit personal-data solicitation but can miss an acceptable action; unlisted and undecided outcomes must remain valid.

The learning question is whether practice could help someone notice a participation condition, distinguish their preference from provision and reconsider a next step. That is a hypothesis. ## Human and system capability

Human requirements: patrons control participation and can express a decision by selection, pointing or speech. They need not explain a choice or demonstrate understanding to receive the fictional materials. An actually available facilitator may read a notice or restate a selection with permission, but must not choose an answer, treat silence as agreement or promise service assistance.

## Experience and decisions

Keep the primary task short, as proposed at sequence 9. Selecting a route reveals its consequence without automatically advancing. For example, staff explanation yields: “Your draft seeks an explanation. In this example, an explanation depends on assistance being available. Real availability and language support are unknown. The mock online route reveals the invented account requirement without offering account or credential fields. Its meaningful decision is whether to inspect the requirement, seek an explanation if support exists, reconsider another route, leave the action unresolved or stop. There is no correct route imposed by the tool.

Recording an initial plan remains optional under sequence 7. An unrecorded initial plan must stay visibly unrecorded. The system does not substitute paper or online practice.

Neighborhood Story Circle remains optional immediate practice. Its invented notice says “Check joining arrangements”; its changed condition is that shared-computer time ends. ## Requirements and rationale

L1 — Preserve a meaningful decision. Origin: Learning scientist, D2.practice; route conditions at sequence 5 and low-burden interaction at sequence 9. Selecting a route must reveal a concrete authored consequence and leave reconsideration under patron control. The human reason is that practice requires a decision whose implications can be inspected; the system reason is to avoid turning selections into a prescribed sequence. Acceptance check: select staff explanation, apply fictional unavailability, then keep, change or leave the action undecided. Each action must produce a faithful description without automatically selecting a substitute or requiring an explanation. Context: the unavailable-staff condition is hypothetical, not a reported incident.

L2 — Use descriptive, correctable feedback. Origin: Learning scientist, D2.practice; correction rules at sequence 7 and participation authority at sequence 9. Describe what changed and which dependency remains. Do not call a route safe, successful, ready or competent. Acceptance check: record staff explanation, change the current route to paper, correct the initial route to undecided, and cancel a further edit. Both plans and feedback must represent those explicit states; no obsolete staff-derived claim or judgment may remain. Human review must separately establish whether the wording is understandable. A technically faithful summary does not establish that the patron understands it.

L3 — Separate practice from demonstrated transfer. Origin: Learning scientist, D4.transfer; optional second situation at sequences 5, 7 and 9, and the parent learning boundary preserved at sequence 2. Label Story Circle as optional practice, not a transfer test. Give it its own notice and device-time condition; offer help on request without penalty. Acceptance check: enter practice, request detail, leave joining arrangements unresolved, revise or stop. No reward, independence label, competence claim or unlocked service appears. The second task must not invent an account requirement. Context: similar route controls and immediate timing may allow interface familiarity to explain performance.

L4 — Keep any later retention inquiry separate. Origin: Learning scientist, D4.transfer; sequence 2 preserves the requirement for a different task and documented support conditions. The candidate must not retain a learning history, schedule follow-up or infer retention from the initial/current comparison. If humans later authorize an inquiry, use a different fictional notice after a review-selected interval and document the conditions of performance: available information, requested and supplied assistance, prior familiarity and interruptions. Acceptance check for this candidate: every output and Help statement distinguishes immediate supported practice from untested later retention and adaptation. Any future inquiry protocol must be reviewed before use; no interval, recruitment or authorization is established here.

L5 — Preserve a complete non-AI practice route. Origin: Learning scientist, D2.practice and D4.transfer; complete packets at sequences 5, 7 and 9. Keep the same notice, condition, choices, correction and refusal available on paper before digital participation. Pointing or speaking is sufficient if an appropriate person is actually available. Acceptance check: a reviewer can conduct the fictional decision using only the packet below, without digital instructions, personal details or a supplied preferred answer. Printing, language access, handling and facilitator workload remain unknown.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Descriptive feedback can support reconsideration but also supply reasoning the patron has not independently produced. Keep wording tied to explicit selections and do not treat accepting the summary as understanding. Fewer suggestions may expose a different support need, but may also increase reading and memory demands; Help must remain available.

Retain dissent that a learning exercise may be unnecessary. Improving the event notice, verifying route information or removing a needless account step could address the service barrier directly. Ordinary conversation with available staff and the following paper packet are non-AI alternatives. Review may favor an alternative or stopping development.

Complete invented paper practice packet:

Card A — Mission and notice. “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Its notice offers morning or afternoon sessions and says ‘Confirm your place.’ Choose a possible next step; this does not register anyone. Use no personal information. Point, speak, mark, pass, pause or stop.”

Card B — Routes and conditions. “Online practice: inspect an invented account requirement; create no account and provide no details. Staff explanation: seek an explanation if suitable assistance exists; real availability and language support are unknown. Paper practice: use these cards; real paper acceptance is unknown. No workable route and undecided are legitimate choices.”

Card C — Optional initial plan. “Route: online / staff explanation / paper practice / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect requirement / seek explanation if support exists / examine another route / wait without a promised time / action not listed / undecided / pause / stop. Support preference: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: another route / undecided / pause / stop.” Leave any item blank. No reason is required.

Card D — Changed condition. “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Keep your preference unresolved, change route, wait without a promised duration, leave undecided, pause or stop. Selecting help does not make it available.”

Card E — Current plan and correction. Repeat Card C for the current plan. “You control continuing. The service owner controls the requirement. Assistance providers control support offered. Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.” Correct either plan by replacing a mark or requesting a restatement. An unrecorded initial plan remains unrecorded. No answer is scored.

Card F — Optional practice and facilitation. “Neighborhood Story Circle is invented. Its notice says ‘Check joining arrangements.’ Those arrangements are unresolved. Choose a possible route and next action using Card C. Imagine shared-computer time ends. Keep, change, pause or stop; review using Card E.” Facilitator script: “Would you like the notice read aloud? Which route, if any? Would you like more detail? Keep or change your choice? Shall I restate it so you can correct it?” Ask permission, accept passing and supply no preferred answer. Before marking cards, agree how they will be handled. Covering conceals paper but does not erase it. This practice establishes no learning or transfer.

## Acceptance checks

L1–L5 are proposed checks, not completed tests. Intended quality is a voluntary, inspectable and correctable decision with clear support boundaries. Technical verification may establish that descriptions match selections, corrections remove stale content and optional practice preserves help. It cannot establish comprehension or learning.

Pending human interaction review must examine whether people can recognize what remains unresolved, whether feedback represents their choice, and whether assistance or reading burden is acceptable. Refusal is valid participation, not a failed task. Preserve contrary interpretations and requested corrections.

Learning, retention and transfer require separate reviewed task evidence. Completion, speed, a changed plan, fewer clicks or fewer prompts are insufficient. Agency, dignity, access, belonging and sustainable workload also require evidence about actual participation conditions; none has been observed.

## Evidence and unknowns

Actual earlier references are sequence 2's preserved context and the drafts at sequences 5, 7 and 9. Embedded historical labels in sequence 2 are not additional event evidence. No human approval or field result is supplied.

After the hypothetical unavailable-staff challenge, feedback must expose the unresolved assistance dependency while preserving patron preference. This contribution adds a learning boundary: revising that preference is inspectable behavior, not evidence of improved capability. Story Circle also retains unknown joining arrangements rather than inheriting the account condition from Drawing Hour.

Rival explanations for apparent ease include prior service familiarity, visible suggestions, repeated controls and facilitator prompting. Difficulty could reflect ambiguous wording, language mismatch, inaccessible controls, interrupted device time or unavailable assistance. Unknowns include whether the exercise is wanted, whether its representations are understood, what support is sustainable, and whether any later adaptation occurs. Field evidence remains pending.

Responsible AI specialist expert draft for Design deliberation in a rehearsal. Nothing here is an approved requirement, participant observation or executed check. Sequence 2 preserves parent Understand, Map and Design context; its embedded historical labels are not additional evidence references. Sequences 5, 7, 9 and 11 are current specialist proposals.

Access Studio invites an adult patron to explore the invented Community Drawing Hour, inspect an authored account requirement and choose a possible next step. Adult patrons, librarians, volunteers, service owners and accessibility practitioners have relevant interests; none participate in this demonstration.

The delegation challenge is that readable synthesis can acquire authority beyond its source choices. A plan saying someone will ask staff can be mistaken for a feasible action, a sent request or an endorsed route. The privacy challenge is that fictional route and support preferences still reveal the exercise participant's selections to nearby people. Absence of personal fields does not by itself establish a discreet handoff.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: the patron decides whether to participate and whether the displayed description represents their choice. Selecting, pointing or speaking are possible ways to express a decision; silence is not agreement. A facilitator must ask permission to read or restate, accept correction and avoid choosing an answer. Suitable assistance must actually exist before oral facilitation can occur.

Service owners control actual event requirements and accepted routes. Assistance providers control the support they offer. Librarians must examine shared-device arrangements, printing and facilitation burden. Patron and practitioner review must examine comprehension, discoverability, privacy and whether the exercise is wanted. These human gates remain unmet.

System requirements: the candidate may display authored information and describe explicit selections. It may not register, contact staff, verify an account, determine eligibility, recommend a consequential route, infer consent or judge capability. Requested support, authored example availability and unknown real provision must remain separate. The task needs no model inference; fixed local rules can generate its descriptive output.

## Experience and decisions

The route board offers mock online practice, staff explanation, complete paper practice and pause or decline. No workable route, undecided and an unlisted next action remain equally legitimate. No personal, account or credential fields are needed.

Each route reveals its consequence and authority boundary beside the choice. Online practice describes the invented account step without creating an account. Staff explanation records a preference and says real assistance and language support are unknown; no request is sent. Paper practice opens complete invented materials and says real paper acceptance is unknown.

Use conditional output: "Your draft seeks an explanation if suitable assistance exists." Avoid "Staff will help you." The review states "Fictional plan; no registration or request sent" next to the generated description. An unset support choice remains "None selected," never "No support needed." Agreeing that text matches a choice establishes only that representation, not comprehension, consent to a service or demonstrated proficiency.

The initial snapshot is optional. Correcting it changes the initial representation; changing the current plan changes the current representation. Cancellation leaves both untouched. Do not retain an additional history of revisions. Unlisted or rejected wording yields an unresolved description without asking for an explanation.

Applying the hypothetical unavailable-staff condition preserves the patron's preference and exposes its unresolved dependency. It offers reconsideration, waiting without a promised duration, remaining undecided, pausing or stopping. It must not silently select paper or online practice. Optional Story Circle practice uses its own notice and device-time condition, with joining arrangements unresolved rather than an inherited account requirement.

## Requirements and rationale

RA1 — Delegation boundary. Origin: Responsible AI specialist, D3.delegation; preference/provision proposals at sequences 5 and 7 and local authority wording at sequence 9. Place the controlling party, fictional condition and unknown real provision beside each route consequence and in the review. Human reason: a patron must be able to distinguish their choice from another party's commitment. System reason: descriptive text must not manufacture provision or authority. Acceptance check: select staff explanation and apply fictional unavailability; the preference persists, assistance remains unresolved, no request is confirmed and no alternative is selected automatically. Context: staffing is unknown and the change is authored, not an observed incident.

RA2 — Accountable representation. Origin: Responsible AI specialist, D3.delegation; correction at sequence 7, voluntary participation at sequence 9 and descriptive feedback at sequence 11. Give distinct controls for correcting the initial plan, changing the current plan and rejecting an unlisted action without free text. Replace dependent descriptions and remove obsolete feedback after correction. Human reason: fluent wording must remain contestable. System reason: every claim must be attributable to explicit selections and stated conditions. Acceptance check: record initial staff preference, change current preference to paper, correct initial preference to undecided and cancel another edit. Both views must reflect those exact choices; no obsolete staff claim, score or assertion of understanding may remain. Comprehension of the comparison is untested.

RA3 — Bounded retention without surveillance. Origin: Responsible AI specialist, D5.privacy; temporary-memory boundary preserved at sequence 2 and bounded snapshots at sequence 7. Keep at most the optional initial snapshot, current draft and state necessary for the active interaction. Do not add a chronological choice log, identifiers, timestamps of patron actions, support-use analytics, exports or inference about independence. Human reason: practice must not become monitoring of patron behavior. System reason: unnecessary retained state increases exposure and clearing complexity. Acceptance check: inspect the implementation for network, telemetry, persistent storage and accumulated action history; inspect reload behavior for absence of restored selections. These checks are pending. A route choice is neither permission to disclose nor evidence of an ability need.

RA4 — Shared-device cover and handoff. Origin: Responsible AI specialist, D5.privacy; complete concealment preserved at sequence 2 and privacy/activity/content separation at sequences 7 and 9. Put Cover, Clear and Stop before task controls in keyboard order. Cover removes all choice-bearing content from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access, including initial/current plans, feedback, pending edits and any displayed paper selections. Focus moves to neutral status. Reveal restores visibility only; resumption remains explicit. Confirmed Clear removes candidate-held choices, snapshots, pending edits and derived messages, then presents a neutral confirmation of that limited scope. It preserves paused or stopped activity and does not create a fresh draft. Cancellation preserves content. Human reason: an interruption must leave usable control over exposure and handoff. System reason: hiding one panel cannot conceal every representation. Acceptance check: exercise these actions from comparison, changed-condition and optional-practice states, including clearing while covered; inspect focus, live announcements and stale content. Covering is concealment, not erasure. No device-wide deletion claim is permitted.

RA5 — Human gates and non-AI equivalence. Origin: Responsible AI specialist, D3.delegation and D5.privacy; human gates preserved at sequence 2, paper route at sequence 5, participation boundaries at sequence 9 and learning limits at sequence 11. Make the complete packet below available before digital participation. No finished plan, explanation or second task is required. Human reason: refusal and alternatives must be usable rather than ceremonial. System reason: a candidate cannot approve its own service fit or privacy adequacy. Acceptance check: a reviewer can conduct the fictional task using only the packet, correct either plan and stop without personal details or a preferred answer. Patron, librarian and practitioner review must separately examine wantedness, language arrangements, handling and workload. Any later pilot requires accountable human review and interaction testing; this draft supplies neither authorization nor approval.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

The optional comparison can make reconsideration visible but retains additional choice-bearing content and adds memory demands. Review may remove it while preserving a correctable current plan. Fixed choices reduce personal disclosure but may omit a desired action; unlisted and undecided outcomes must remain valid.

Retain dissent that improving the notice or removing needless service friction could address the underlying problem more directly. A static authored route board, the paper packet and conversation with actually available staff are non-AI alternatives. None establishes operational access. Reviewers may prefer an alternative or stop development.

Complete invented paper/facilitation packet:

Card A — Mission and notice. "Community Drawing Hour is fictional. Its notice offers morning or afternoon sessions and says ‘Confirm your place.’ Explore a possible next step; this does not register anyone. Use no personal information. Point, speak, mark, pass, pause or stop. Session preference is optional."

Card B — Routes and conditions. "Online practice: inspect an invented account requirement; create no account and provide no details. Staff explanation: seek an explanation if suitable assistance exists; real availability and language support are unknown. Paper practice: use these cards; real service acceptance of paper is unknown. No workable route and undecided are legitimate choices."

Card C — Optional initial plan. "Route: online practice / staff explanation / paper practice / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect requirement / seek explanation if assistance exists / examine another route / wait without a promised duration / action not listed / undecided / pause / stop. Support preference: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: examine another route / remain undecided / pause / stop." Leave any item blank. No reason is required. None selected does not establish that support is unnecessary.

Card D — Changed condition. "Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Keep your preference unresolved, change route, wait without a promised duration, leave undecided, pause or stop. Choosing assistance does not make it available."

Card E — Current plan and correction. Repeat Card C's choices for the current plan. "You control continuing. The service owner controls the requirement. Assistance providers control offered support. Fictional plan; no registration or request sent." Identify whether a correction changes the initial or current plan. Replace a mark or request a restatement. An unrecorded initial plan stays unrecorded; no answer is scored.

Card F — Handling and facilitation. "Before marking, agree who may see the cards and how they will be handled afterward. Leave them unmarked if preferred. Folding or covering conceals them; it does not erase them." Facilitator script: "Would you like to point, speak, mark, pass or stop? May I read the notice? Which route, if any? Would you like the imagined change? May I restate your selection so you can correct it?" Wait for an explicit response; collect no personal details, promise no service assistance and infer no understanding. Facilitation depends on an actually available person.

Optional practice card — "Neighborhood Story Circle is fictional. Its notice says ‘Check joining arrangements’; those arrangements remain unresolved. Use Card C to choose a possible route and next action. Imagine shared-computer time ends. Keep, revise, pause or stop; review with Card E. More explanation is available on request if an appropriate facilitator exists. This practice establishes no learning or transfer."

## Acceptance checks

RA1–RA5 describe proposed observable checks. Intended quality is an understandable, voluntary and correctable decision with honest authority boundaries and usable privacy controls. No technical behavior has been observed and no check has been executed.

Technical verification must inspect all reachable privacy and correction states, keyboard focus, reflow, announcements, stale content and absence of network, storage, telemetry, personal fields and external navigation. Passing those checks would establish only the tested behavior, not privacy in every device environment or accessibility certification.

Affected-person and practitioner review must separately examine whether wording implies provision, whether a patron can reject a summary, whether refusal feels legitimate and whether concealment and clearing are discoverable during interruption. Learning, transfer, agency, dignity, access, belonging and sustainable workload remain untested. Completion, speed or fewer prompts cannot establish those outcomes.

## Evidence and unknowns

Sequence 2 is the supplied preservation event, not a privacy incident or newly verified finding. Sequences 5, 7, 9 and 11 provide draft proposals. They contain no participant observations, human approval or field results. Field evidence remains pending.

After the hypothetical unavailable-staff challenge, the requirement changes from presenting help as an ordinary next step to preserving a preference with an unresolved provision dependency. This contribution additionally constrains the authority of generated wording and the exposure of snapshots, pending edits and feedback during handoff. These refine current Design; no earlier artifact revision is requested.

Rival explanations for difficulty include ambiguous notices, language mismatch, inaccessible controls, interrupted device time and unavailable assistance. Apparent ease could reflect prior familiarity, visible suggestions or facilitator steering. Unknowns include whether the exercise is wanted, actual routes, account necessity, paper acceptance, staffing, language arrangements, shared-device behavior and acceptable support workload.

## Next decision

REVISION AND SCOPE
Revise Design once: replace nominal reachability with explicit placement, reflow and focus requirements. The dependency model and problem frame remain applicable; the earliest artifact needing this change is Design. The unresolved Understand human-review gate remains pending, without requesting another revision of Understand.

SCREEN ORDER AND ACCESS
Place a short strip labeled “Privacy and stopping” before planning content and first among interactive controls in keyboard order. Use neutral buttons: “Conceal draft,” “Clear draft,” and “Stop exercise.” Keep applicable actions accessible during active, paused, stopped and concealed states; clearing must remain available without revealing content.
The layout must wrap controls without horizontal scrolling, clipping or overlap at magnification settings selected through human review. Any persistent positioning must not obscure controls, focused elements or task content. Review must examine discoverability from within the planning area, not merely from the initial screen. Do not rely on assumed shortcuts, devices or staff intervention. These are requirements to verify, not accessibility claims.

FICTIONAL PLANNING CONTENT
Opening: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Its notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Real routes and assistance availability are unknown. Use fictional choices only.”
Approach choices: consider online; check for paper; check for staffed help; availability unknown; none works; undecided. Next-action choices: examine the notice; ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available; check another route; my action is not listed; undecided. Both default to undecided. No explanation is required for a missing action.
“Describe my draft” optionally presents fixed text describing current selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” Visible descriptions update immediately after correction. No preferred route, praise, score or completion judgment is allowed.

PRIVACY AND FOCUS TRANSITIONS
Conceal hides selectors, descriptions and all choice-specific messages, including interruption output, from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access. Move focus to a neutral status: “Fictional content remains in this session.” Provide explicit reveal, clear and stop controls. Reveal restores visibility only; it must not resume activity automatically or announce a choice-specific summary.
Clear removes candidate-held choices, descriptions and choice-specific messages. Move focus to: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Preserve paused or stopped activity. Do not recreate a draft automatically. A new undecided draft requires explicit action; resuming also requires explicit action. Focus destinations must remain available and understandable without exposing choices.
Use temporary current-draft memory only: no free text, history, analytics, persistent storage, exports, transmissions or automatic staff requests. All implementation boundaries require verification.

OPTIONAL CHANGE AND RECOVERY
Offer separate invitations to try a confusing notice or rehearse an interruption. Neither unlocks assistance or finishing. Confusion repeats that confirmation and help availability remain unresolved. Interruption states: “Imagine the shared-computer session ends before you continue,” and pauses activity. Offer keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; privacy controls remain available. No automatic recovery or inferred intention is permitted. If draft loss is known, disclose it and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices.

NON-AI COMPARISON
Prepare a paper card with the same notice, approach and action choices, correction, uncertainty, pause and stop. Pointing or speaking is sufficient; writing is optional and fictional only. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it; discreet handling needs review. Ordinary conversation with available staff and clearer service notices remain alternatives. Staff capacity is unknown; reviewers may prefer an alternative or reject the tool.

REVIEW AND NEXT ACTION

Proposed checks cover keyboard discovery during interruption, magnified reflow, neutral focus, complete concealment, stale descriptions, clear while stopped, and storage/transmission boundaries. None has been performed.
Accountable patron and librarian review must examine framing, access, privacy, missing actions and workload before approved design. Integrated Model artifact for public deliberation in a rehearsal; requirements remain provisional. Sequences 4 and 6 identify service barriers and meaningful refusal. Sequence 8 incorporates those into Understand. Sequence 13 separates plan preference from provision and challenges incomplete concealment. No participant observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. Modeling does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate.

PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY
Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action.

DEPENDENCY MODEL
A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning.

STATE MODEL
Maintain independent fields:
Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided.
Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability.
Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action.
Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion.

REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS
Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan.
Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise.

ADOPTED MODEL REVISION
Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame.

LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK
A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed.

NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS
Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. Review may favor an alternative or reject all candidates.

EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES — PENDING
Proposed comparison questions: Can reviewers find an acceptable action, including stopping? Do labels imply provision? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens arise? Can fictional content be corrected, concealed completely and cleared after interruption? Retain contrary accounts and distinguish task familiarity, reviewer prompting and service barriers from any learning explanation. Completion and speed are insufficient evidence.
Unknowns include route existence, staffing windows, language arrangements, accessibility needs, shared-device behavior and demand for this tool. Accountable patron and librarian review must address framing, privacy, access and workload before approved design or a pilot. Subsequent technical checks and human interaction testing remain required. No recruitment, review, launch or efficacy is asserted.

NEXT ACTION
Use this model to prepare a small screen outline, matching paper card and dependency questions sheet for review. Keep any subsequent Design work explicitly provisional until the unresolved human gate is met.","content_hash":"20628f8a6e48e1f171f619d20e4a92c67f0dc7e5298c432211ff53d3709df9b5","revision":1},"understand":{"body":"STATUS AND BASIS

Sequence 6 challenges the assumption that three offered routes constitute meaningful choice. The seed supplies the fictional task and restrictions. No participant observations, human approvals or field results exist.

PROBLEM FRAME
Investigate what enables adults to choose an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service while retaining control, privacy and manageable effort. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping.

ADOPTED REVISION

System reason: the candidate cannot approve service fit or supply staffing. Check: a reviewer can conduct notice inspection, choice, change, correction and refusal using only the packet, without personal information or a preferred answer. Progressive detail reduces initial reading but risks hiding dependencies, so essential conditions stay visible. Optional comparison makes reconsideration inspectable but adds state, privacy exposure and memory demands; review may remove it while retaining a correctable current plan. Fixed choices avoid personal disclosure but omit possibilities, so unlisted and unresolved outcomes remain valid.

Retain dissent: clearer notices, verified route information or removal of unnecessary account friction may solve the problem more directly. A static authored route board, the complete paper packet and conversation with actually available staff are non-AI alternatives. The proposed digital candidate itself needs no AI inference. Complete invented paper/facilitation packet follows. It requires no digital interface and does not establish real service acceptance.

Card A — Mission and notice. “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Morning and afternoon sessions are offered; materials are provided in this example. The notice says ‘Confirm your place.’ Explore a possible next step; this does not register anyone. Use no personal information. Point, speak, mark, pass, pause or stop. Card B — Routes and conditions. “Online practice: inspect an invented account step before confirmation; create no account and provide no details. Staff explanation: seek an explanation if suitable assistance exists; real availability and language support are unknown. Paper practice: use these cards; real service acceptance of paper is unknown. No workable route and undecided are legitimate choices. You control continuing; the service owner controls requirements; assistance providers control offered support.”

Card C — Optional initial plan. “Route: online practice / staff explanation / paper practice / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect requirement / seek explanation if assistance exists / examine another route / wait without a promised duration / action not listed / undecided / pause / stop. Support preference: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: examine another route / remain undecided / pause / stop.” Leave any item blank. None selected does not establish that support is unnecessary. Record an initial plan only if wanted.

Card D — Changed condition. “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Your preference does not make help available. Keep it unresolved, change route, wait without a promised duration, remain undecided, pause or stop.” This is an imagined condition, not a service report.

Card E — Current plan and correction. Repeat Card C’s choices for the current plan, noting whether Card D was used. “Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.” To correct, identify initial or current, replace the chosen mark or request a restatement, and check the corresponding description. The initial plan keeps its original condition context. An unrecorded initial plan stays unrecorded. No reason or answer score is required.

Card F — Handling and facilitation. “Before marking, agree who may see the cards and how they will be handled afterward. Leave them unmarked if preferred. Folding or covering conceals; it does not erase.” Facilitator script: “Would you like to point, speak, mark, pass or stop? May I read the notice? Which route, if any? Would you like the imagined change? May I restate your selection so you can correct it?” Await explicit permission; collect no personal information, select no preferred answer and promise no assistance. Oral facilitation depends on an actually available person.

Optional practice card — “Neighborhood Story Circle is invented. Its notice says ‘Check joining arrangements.’ The arrangements remain unresolved. Choose online inspection of this notice, conditional staff explanation, paper practice, no workable route or undecided. Use Card C for your next action and support preference. Imagine shared-computer time ends; pause without changing preference. Keep, revise or stop; review with Card E. There is no stated account requirement. More detail is optional. R1–R7 specify proposed observable checks; none has been executed. Intended quality is a voluntary, understandable, correctable decision with honest dependencies. There is currently no implemented candidate or observed technical behavior in this contribution.

Technical verification must exercise correction, cancellation, replacement, interruption, concealment, clearing and reload across relevant states, including focus, announcements and narrow or magnified layouts. It must inspect prohibited data collection and external activity. Passing a check establishes only the behavior exercised.

Human interaction review must separately examine wantedness, comprehension, refusal, language arrangements, privacy discoverability and support burden. Completion, speed, a changed plan or fewer prompts establish neither learning nor later transfer.

## Evidence and unknowns

Evidence references are the actual supplied preservation event at sequence 2 and draft contributions at sequences 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. Historical sequence labels embedded in the parent are background, not additional event citations. No human approvals, participant observations, measured outcomes or executed checks exist.

What changes after the hypothetical staff-unavailability condition: staff preference persists while the example assistance dependency becomes unresolved; reconsideration is offered without route substitution. Specialist challenges additionally make comparison optional, feedback descriptive, authority local, state bounded and Story Circle task-specific. These changes refine current Design without invalidating an earlier artifact.

Unknowns include demand, actual routes, account necessity, staffing, paper acceptance, language arrangements, shared-device behavior and sustainable workload. Rival explanations include service design, language mismatch, access barriers and interruptions; familiarity and prompting could explain apparent ease. Field pilot, learning, retention, transfer and flourishing evidence remain pending.

Use this screen outline and complete packet as the concrete Design review package. Retain the parent human gates and seek pending patron, librarian, service-owner and accessibility-practitioner review of relevance, authority, refusal, access, privacy and workload, preserving dissent and corrections. A subsequent Build may create a local rehearsal candidate for technical and interaction review; this brief grants no operational approval or pilot authorization. Decide after review whether to simplify comparison, choose a non-AI service improvement, continue candidate development or stop.
