Optional comparison makes reconsideration inspectable but adds state, privacy exposure and memory demands; review may remove it while retaining a correctable current plan. Fixed choices avoid personal disclosure but omit possibilities, so unlisted and unresolved outcomes remain valid.

Retain dissent: clearer notices, verified route information or removal of unnecessary account friction may solve the problem more directly. A static authored route board, the complete paper packet and conversation with actually available staff are non-AI alternatives. The proposed digital candidate itself needs no AI inference. Reviewers may prefer an alternative or stop development.

Complete invented paper/facilitation packet follows. It requires no digital interface and does not establish real service acceptance.

Card A — Mission and notice. “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Morning and afternoon sessions are offered; materials are provided in this example. The notice says ‘Confirm your place.’ Explore a possible next step; this does not register anyone. Use no personal information. Point, speak, mark, pass, pause or stop. Session preference is optional.”

Card B — Routes and conditions. “Online practice: inspect an invented account step before confirmation; create no account and provide no details. Staff explanation: seek an explanation if suitable assistance exists; real availability and language support are unknown. Paper practice: use these cards; real service acceptance of paper is unknown. No workable route and undecided are legitimate choices. You control continuing; the service owner controls requirements; assistance providers control offered support.”

Card C — Optional initial plan. “Route: online practice / staff explanation / paper practice / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect requirement / seek explanation if assistance exists / examine another route / wait without a promised duration / action not listed / undecided / pause / stop. Support preference: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: examine another route / remain undecided / pause / stop.” Leave any item blank. None selected does not establish that support is unnecessary. Record an initial plan only if wanted.

Card D — Changed condition. “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Your preference does not make help available. Keep it unresolved, change route, wait without a promised duration, remain undecided, pause or stop.” This is an imagined condition, not a service report.

Card E — Current plan and correction. Repeat Card C’s choices for the current plan, noting whether Card D was used. “Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.” To correct, identify initial or current, replace the chosen mark or request a restatement, and check the corresponding description. The initial plan keeps its original condition context. An unrecorded initial plan stays unrecorded. No reason or answer score is required.

Card F — Handling and facilitation. “Before marking, agree who may see the cards and how they will be handled afterward. Leave them unmarked if preferred. Folding or covering conceals; it does not erase.” Facilitator script: “Would you like to point, speak, mark, pass or stop? May I read the notice? Which route, if any? Would you like the imagined change? May I restate your selection so you can correct it?” Await explicit permission; collect no personal information, select no preferred answer and promise no assistance. Oral facilitation depends on an actually available person.

Optional practice card — “Neighborhood Story Circle is invented. Its notice says ‘Check joining arrangements.’ The arrangements remain unresolved. Choose online inspection of this notice, conditional staff explanation, paper practice, no workable route or undecided. Use Card C for your next action and support preference. Imagine shared-computer time ends; pause without changing preference. Keep, revise or stop; review with Card E. There is no stated account requirement. More detail is optional. This practice establishes no learning or transfer.”

## Acceptance checks

R1–R7 specify proposed observable checks; none has been executed. Intended quality is a voluntary, understandable, correctable decision with honest dependencies. There is currently no implemented candidate or observed technical behavior in this contribution.

Technical verification must exercise correction, cancellation, replacement, interruption, concealment, clearing and reload across relevant states, including focus, announcements and narrow or magnified layouts. It must inspect prohibited data collection and external activity. Passing a check establishes only the behavior exercised.

Human interaction review must separately examine wantedness, comprehension, refusal, language arrangements, privacy discoverability and support burden. Agency includes rejecting a plan; dignity excludes deficit labels; access and belonging depend on actual conditions; sustainable workload includes facilitation and paper handling. Completion, speed, a changed plan or fewer prompts establish neither learning nor later transfer.

## Evidence and unknowns

Evidence references are the actual supplied preservation event at sequence 2 and draft contributions at sequences 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. Historical sequence labels embedded in the parent are background, not additional event citations. No human approvals, participant observations, measured outcomes or executed checks exist.

What changes after the hypothetical staff-unavailability condition: staff preference persists while the example assistance dependency becomes unresolved; reconsideration is offered without route substitution. Specialist challenges additionally make comparison optional, feedback descriptive, authority local, state bounded and Story Circle task-specific. These changes refine current Design without invalidating an earlier artifact.

Unknowns include demand, actual routes, account necessity, staffing, paper acceptance, language arrangements, shared-device behavior and sustainable workload. Rival explanations include service design, language mismatch, access barriers and interruptions; familiarity and prompting could explain apparent ease. Field pilot, learning, retention, transfer and flourishing evidence remain pending.

## Next decision

Use this screen outline and complete packet as the concrete Design review package. Retain the parent human gates and seek pending patron, librarian, service-owner and accessibility-practitioner review of relevance, authority, refusal, access, privacy and workload, preserving dissent and corrections. A subsequent Build may create a local rehearsal candidate for technical and interaction review; this brief grants no operational approval or pilot authorization. Decide after review whether to simplify comparison, choose a non-AI service improvement, continue candidate development or stop.

The stronger journey changes the current Design; the parent problem frame and Map dependency account remain applicable. Their human-review gates remain unresolved.

Apparent ease could reflect prior familiarity, repeated controls or facilitator prompting.

## Human and system capability

Passing and declining require no reason. An actually available facilitator may read authored information or restate selections with permission, but must not choose an answer, infer understanding or promise service assistance.

Service owners control actual event requirements and accepted routes. Assistance providers control support offered; device operators affect session conditions. Librarians must assess printing, shared-device arrangements and facilitation workload. Patron, librarian, service-owner and practitioner review must establish wantedness, appropriate language arrangements and feasible support before operational use. None is presumed available or authorized.

System requirements: separate explicit patron preference, authored example conditions, unknown real provision and the chosen next action. The candidate can expose dependencies and describe selections; it cannot register, contact staff, create accounts, establish eligibility, reserve help or judge capability. Fixed local rules suffice; model inference is unnecessary. Use no personal, credential or account fields, free text, scores, deficit labels, network calls, storage, telemetry, external assets, links or real submissions.

The coupled requirement is conditional: a desired action may require understandable information, a usable route, device time and suitable assistance. Selecting a route cannot create those conditions. Information about authority and unresolved provision must appear beside the decision, not only in Help.

## Hypothetical event and challenged assumption

Scenario specialist expert draft for public deliberation. Imagine the prepared paper packets run out during the fictional Community Drawing Hour exercise. A fictional patron objects: “I chose paper so I could leave the screen. Showing me cards on this screen does not give me that route.” This is one authored scenario, not a participant quotation or reported incident.

Sequence 5 proposes complete paper materials; sequence 7 requires a reviewer to conduct the exercise using only the packet; sequence 15 integrates equivalent alternatives into R7. The current Design supplies complete content and acknowledges unknown printing capacity. Its unresolved delivery assumption is that making that content available in the candidate suffices to offer screen-independent paper practice. Content completeness and physical availability are separate conditions.

## Requested requirement change

Revise Design R7 to distinguish “View the paper materials” from “Use a prepared paper packet.” Viewing opens the complete authored content without claiming a physical packet exists. Paper preference remains selectable regardless of provision. Real packet availability, usable format and service acceptance remain separately unknown.

For this hypothetical condition, show beside the paper consequence: “In this example, prepared packets have run out. The materials can be viewed here, but a physical paper route is unresolved. No printing or replenishment is arranged.” Preserve the selected paper preference. Offer retaining it unresolved, reconsidering another route, leaving undecided or stopping; do not select screen practice automatically. Do not require a reason or personal information.

Before any later facilitated paper exercise, an accountable human provider must establish that complete usable materials exist independently of the candidate, including the notice, conditions, choices, correction and refusal instructions already supplied. This is a proposed readiness requirement, not an authorization or promise of printing, staffing or accessible formats. Screen-only delivery must not be described as an equivalent offline route.

Origin: Scenario agent, D1.coupling, D3.agency and D4.verification, challenging the paper-equivalence proposals at sequences 5, 7 and 15. Human reason: a patron controls their preference but cannot create materials or accept another medium by implication. System reason: route preference, delivery conditions and service acceptance must produce distinct descriptive claims.

## Observable acceptance checks

Select paper practice, optionally record an initial plan, then apply the fictional exhausted-supply condition. The preference must persist while the current plan marks physical provision unresolved. Viewing content must not change that condition or confirm a usable paper route.

Change the current route and cancel a subsequent correction. Initial and current descriptions must retain their respective condition contexts, remove stale dependent wording after committed corrections and preserve committed choices after cancellation. These are proposed checks; none has run.

Separately, a reviewer given the prepared packet must be able to perform notice inspection, reconsideration, correction and refusal without the screen. If no packet is supplied, that delivery check remains unmet; displaying its text cannot count as passing it. Patron and practitioner usability review remains pending.

## Alternatives, dissent and uncertainty

A prepared static route board and the complete existing paper packet are non-AI options. An ordinary explanation depends on an actually available person. Retain dissent that better notices or removal of unnecessary account friction could address the problem more directly, and that no exercise may be wanted.

Rival explanations for rejecting the digital route include device usability, language or format mismatch, interruption, privacy concerns and ordinary medium preference. None establishes a learning deficit. Unknowns include supply arrangements, replenishment capacity, accessible formats, handling privacy and whether patrons want the task. Field evidence, learning, transfer and flourishing remain pending.

## Next decision

Request revision of the current Design’s R7 wording, delivery dependency and acceptance checks before representing paper practice as equivalent. The earliest invalidated artifact is Design: the supplied Map framing already treats provision as conditional and does not require revision. Preserve the existing complete packet and unresolved human gates. No operational approval is supplied.

CURRENT ARTIFACTS: {"design":{"content":{"body":"## Problem and people

Access Studio: choose a route, keep control is a fictional community-event participation exercise. Its task is to explore an invented notice, inspect a participation condition and decide an acceptable next step. Independent online completion is not the objective. An unresolved plan, paper practice, conditional assistance, passing or stopping is legitimate.

Relevant people are adult patrons with varied reading, languages and device access; librarians, volunteers, service owners and accessibility practitioners. None participates in this rehearsal. This is an integrated provisional Design artifact, not an approved requirement set.

Sequence 2 is the supplied verification event preserving the immutable parent Understand, Map and Design records. I acknowledge its instruction to refine Design without rerunning earlier stages unless a named requirement is invalidated. It records preservation, not a newly observed problem or successful check. The stronger journey changes the current Design; the parent problem frame and Map dependency account remain applicable. Their human-review gates remain unresolved.

The problem may be service friction rather than a learning need: an unnecessary account step, ambiguous notice, inaccessible route, language mismatch, interrupted device time or absent assistance could explain difficulty. Apparent ease could reflect prior familiarity, repeated controls or facilitator prompting.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: patrons control continuing, choosing support and correcting how their choices are represented. Selecting, pointing or speaking can express a decision; silence is not agreement. Passing and declining require no reason. An actually available facilitator may read authored information or restate selections with permission, but must not choose an answer, infer understanding or promise service assistance.

Service owners control actual event requirements and accepted routes. Assistance providers control support offered; device operators affect session conditions. Librarians must assess printing, shared-device arrangements and facilitation workload. Patron, librarian, service-owner and practitioner review must establish wantedness, appropriate language arrangements and feasible support before operational use. None is presumed available or authorized.

System requirements: separate explicit patron preference, authored example conditions, unknown real provision and the chosen next action. The candidate can expose dependencies and describe selections; it cannot register, contact staff, create accounts, establish eligibility, reserve help or judge capability. Fixed local rules suffice; model inference is unnecessary. Use no personal, credential or account fields, free text, scores, deficit labels, network calls, storage, telemetry, external assets, links or real submissions.

The coupled requirement is conditional: a desired action may require understandable information, a usable route, device time and suitable assistance. Selecting a route cannot create those conditions. Information about authority and unresolved provision must appear beside the decision, not only in Help.

## Experience and decisions

Opening mission: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Explore its example notice and choose a possible next step. This exercise cannot register anyone. Use fictional choices only.” The notice offers morning and afternoon sessions, says materials are provided in this example, and asks patrons to “Confirm your place.” Session preference is optional and never a reservation. Real routes, assistance and language support remain unknown.

A small illustrated route board carries complete text labels: Explore the event, Choose a route, Check a condition, Review your plan. Illustrations add orientation only. The meaningful main task is one route choice followed by inspection of its consequence. No full worksheet or completed sequence is required.

Offer mock online practice, staff explanation and paper practice, alongside Pause, Decline, No route works for me and Leave undecided. No route is preselected. Route selection reveals a short consequence without advancing automatically. Pause and Decline change activity explicitly; they do not silently replace a route preference. Essential fiction, provision and control statements remain visible when More detail is closed.

Online practice reveals: “This invented portal includes an account step before confirmation. No account is created here.” Local controls allow inspecting that requirement, seeking an explanation if assistance exists, reconsidering another route or stopping. There are no account, password, identifier or contact fields. Staff explanation yields: “Your draft seeks an explanation if suitable assistance exists. Real availability and language support are unknown. No request is sent.” Paper practice opens the complete packet below; real acceptance of paper remains unknown. Unlisted actions can remain unresolved without text entry.

The current plan is available without recording a baseline. Optional “Keep this as my initial plan” captures the current explicit choices and their authored condition context. Otherwise show “Initial plan not recorded.” Support and fallback choices are optional; “None selected” never becomes “No support needed.” The plan describes route, next action, support preference, controlling party and fallback, with “Fictional plan; no registration or request sent” adjacent to the output.

Invite the hypothetical change: “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit.” Applying it preserves the preference and marks assistance unresolved under that example condition. It never alters unknown real provision. Offer keeping the preference, changing route, waiting without a promised duration, leaving undecided, pausing or stopping. Descriptive feedback identifies the explicit change and remaining condition; it provides no praise or preferred answer.

Before/Now comparison is optional. Correct initial plan edits the recorded initial choices using their original condition context; Change current plan edits current choices. Both identify the side being edited. Cancel preserves committed choices. Corrections replace dependent wording rather than accumulating a history. An absent initial snapshot cannot be reconstructed or silently created.

Optional Neighborhood Story Circle practice has its own invented notice: “Check joining arrangements.” Those arrangements remain unresolved; it inherits no Drawing Hour account requirement. Its authored change is “Imagine your shared-computer time ends,” which pauses activity without changing preference. Offer fewer initial suggestions while keeping Help, paper, correction, passing and stopping equally reachable. Task replacement explains that it clears the previous task draft and offers Cancel before replacement.

Cover, Clear and Stop precede task controls in keyboard order. Cover conceals all choice-bearing content and pending edits, moves focus to neutral status and explicitly pauses an active exercise; a stopped exercise stays stopped. Reveal restores visibility only. Resume is a separate action. Stop retains temporary content until cleared and makes privacy controls available. Confirmed Clear removes all candidate-held task choices, snapshots, condition selections, pending edits and derived messages; it preserves covered, paused or stopped status and creates no new draft. A fresh undecided draft requires an explicit action. Reload restores no prior choices.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Route and provision honesty. Origin: Public library domain specialist, sequence 5, D1.problem and D5.context; Systems engineer, sequence 7, D1.coupling; Responsible AI specialist, sequence 13, D3.delegation. Preserve the Map distinction acknowledged in sequence 2. Each route reveals its authored condition, controlling party and unknown real provision. Human reason: a preference must not become another party’s commitment. System reason: assistance availability is independent of route selection. Check: select staff explanation and apply fictional unavailability; preference persists, the dependency becomes unresolved, no request is confirmed and alternatives remain selectable. Actual staffing and paper acceptance are unknown.

R2 — Low-burden practice and feedback. Origin: Human-centered designer, sequence 9, D2.prototyping and D5.context; Learning scientist, sequence 11, D2.practice. One route choice reveals a concrete consequence; additional selectors, baseline and change practice remain optional. Longer explanations can be closed without losing the decision. Human reason: participation must not require a finished plan. System reason: route inspection is a coherent task without mandatory data collection. Check: inspect the account condition and leave next action undecided without validation errors, forced progression or completion judgment. Acceptable wording and burden require patron review.

R3 — Agency and contestable synthesis. Origin: Human-centered designer, sequence 9, D3.agency; Systems engineer, sequence 7, D4.verification; Responsible AI specialist, sequence 13, D3.delegation. Offer passing, no workable route, undecided and unlisted action with neutral visual weight. Separate initial correction from current changes, and derive descriptions only from explicit choices and each side’s condition context. Human reason: fluent wording must remain rejectable. System reason: corrections must remove stale dependent claims. Check: record initial staff preference, change current route to paper, correct initial route to undecided and cancel another edit; both sides remain faithful, including support left unselected. Comprehension is untested.

R4 — Access and shared-device recovery. Origin: Systems engineer, sequence 7, D1.coupling and D4.verification; Human-centered designer, sequence 9, D2.prototyping and D5.context; Responsible AI specialist, sequence 13, D5.privacy; explicit focus requirements preserved in sequence 2. Provide text alternatives, visible focus, responsive reflow and predictable focus restoration. Keep visibility, activity and content presence separately represented. Human reason: interruption must preserve control over exposure and continuation. System reason: concealing one summary is insufficient. Check: cover from comparison, change and practice views; inspect visual, keyboard and assistive-technology concealment, including announcements. Reveal must not resume. Cancel clearing must preserve content; confirmed clearing while covered or stopped must remove every task representation, preserve activity and focus a neutral confirmation. No device-wide erasure or accessibility certification is claimed.

R5 — Bounded state and delegated authority. Origin: Responsible AI specialist, sequence 13, D3.delegation and D5.privacy; Systems engineer, sequence 7, D4.verification. Keep only the current draft, optional initial snapshot and temporary state necessary for editing and activity. Use authored rules without histories, exports, analytics or inference. Human reason: a support preference must not become surveillance or consent. System reason: bounded state makes correction and clearing inspectable. Check the candidate for prohibited fields, network, storage, telemetry, external navigation and accumulated action logs; reload must restore no draft. All inspection remains pending.

R6 — Practice and evidence boundaries. Origin: Learning scientist, sequence 11, D4.evidence and D4.transfer; optional practice proposed at sequences 5, 7 and 9. Story Circle uses its own unresolved joining notice and device-time change, with help retained. Human reason: support remains legitimate and immediate practice is not demonstrated transfer. System reason: task-specific data must not leak across replacement. Check: enter practice, request detail, leave arrangements unresolved and stop; no account requirement, score, reward, independence claim or unlocked service appears. Later retention or adaptation requires a separately reviewed task, timing and documented support conditions; none is authorized here.

R7 — Equivalent alternatives and accountable review. Origin: Domain specialist, sequence 5, D1.problem and D5.context; Learning scientist, sequence 11, D2.practice; Responsible AI specialist, sequence 13, D3.delegation and D5.privacy. Make the complete paper packet available before digital participation. Human reason: paper, oral assistance and stopping must be usable choices. System reason: the candidate cannot approve service fit or supply staffing. Check: a reviewer can conduct notice inspection, choice, change, correction and refusal using only the packet, without personal information or a preferred answer. Practitioner and affected-person review must examine language, handling and workload; field evidence remains pending.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Progressive detail reduces initial reading but risks hiding dependencies, so essential conditions stay visible. Optional comparison makes reconsideration inspectable but adds state, privacy exposure and memory demands; review may remove it while retaining a correctable current plan. Fixed choices avoid personal disclosure but omit possibilities, so unlisted and unresolved outcomes remain valid.

Retain dissent: clearer notices, verified route information or removal of unnecessary account friction may solve the problem more directly. A static authored route board, the complete paper packet and conversation with actually available staff are non-AI alternatives. The proposed digital candidate itself needs no AI inference. Reviewers may prefer an alternative or stop development.

Complete invented paper/facilitation packet follows. It requires no digital interface and does not establish real service acceptance.

Card A — Mission and notice. “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Morning and afternoon sessions are offered; materials are provided in this example. The notice says ‘Confirm your place.’ Explore a possible next step; this does not register anyone. Use no personal information. Point, speak, mark, pass, pause or stop. Session preference is optional.”

Card B — Routes and conditions. “Online practice: inspect an invented account step before confirmation; create no account and provide no details. Staff explanation: seek an explanation if suitable assistance exists; real availability and language support are unknown. Paper practice: use these cards; real service acceptance of paper is unknown. No workable route and undecided are legitimate choices. You control continuing; the service owner controls requirements; assistance providers control offered support.”

Card C — Optional initial plan. “Route: online practice / staff explanation / paper practice / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect requirement / seek explanation if assistance exists / examine another route / wait without a promised duration / action not listed / undecided / pause / stop. Support preference: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: examine another route / remain undecided / pause / stop.” Leave any item blank. None selected does not establish that support is unnecessary. Record an initial plan only if wanted.

Card D — Changed condition. “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Your preference does not make help available. Keep it unresolved, change route, wait without a promised duration, remain undecided, pause or stop.” This is an imagined condition, not a service report.

Card E — Current plan and correction. Repeat Card C’s choices for the current plan, noting whether Card D was used. “Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.” To correct, identify initial or current, replace the chosen mark or request a restatement, and check the corresponding description. The initial plan keeps its original condition context. An unrecorded initial plan stays unrecorded. No reason or answer score is required.

Card F — Handling and facilitation. “Before marking, agree who may see the cards and how they will be handled afterward. Leave them unmarked if preferred. Folding or covering conceals; it does not erase.” Facilitator script: “Would you like to point, speak, mark, pass or stop? May I read the notice? Which route, if any? Would you like the imagined change? May I restate your selection so you can correct it?” Await explicit permission; collect no personal information, select no preferred answer and promise no assistance. Oral facilitation depends on an actually available person.

Optional practice card — “Neighborhood Story Circle is invented. Its notice says ‘Check joining arrangements.’ The arrangements remain unresolved. Choose online inspection of this notice, conditional staff explanation, paper practice, no workable route or undecided. Use Card C for your next action and support preference. Imagine shared-computer time ends; pause without changing preference. Keep, revise or stop; review with Card E. There is no stated account requirement. More detail is optional. This practice establishes no learning or transfer.”

## Acceptance checks

R1–R7 specify proposed observable checks; none has been executed. Intended quality is a voluntary, understandable, correctable decision with honest dependencies. There is currently no implemented candidate or observed technical behavior in this contribution.

Technical verification must exercise correction, cancellation, replacement, interruption, concealment, clearing and reload across relevant states, including focus, announcements and narrow or magnified layouts. It must inspect prohibited data collection and external activity. Passing a check establishes only the behavior exercised.

Human interaction review must separately examine wantedness, comprehension, refusal, language arrangements, privacy discoverability and support burden. Agency includes rejecting a plan; dignity excludes deficit labels; access and belonging depend on actual conditions; sustainable workload includes facilitation and paper handling. Completion, speed, a changed plan or fewer prompts establish neither learning nor later transfer.

## Evidence and unknowns

Evidence references are the actual supplied preservation event at sequence 2 and draft contributions at sequences 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. Historical sequence labels embedded in the parent are background, not additional event citations. No human approvals, participant observations, measured outcomes or executed checks exist.

What changes after the hypothetical staff-unavailability condition: staff preference persists while the example assistance dependency becomes unresolved; reconsideration is offered without route substitution. Specialist challenges additionally make comparison optional, feedback descriptive, authority local, state bounded and Story Circle task-specific. These changes refine current Design without invalidating an earlier artifact.

Unknowns include demand, actual routes, account necessity, staffing, paper acceptance, language arrangements, shared-device behavior and sustainable workload. Rival explanations include service design, language mismatch, access barriers and interruptions; familiarity and prompting could explain apparent ease. Field pilot, learning, retention, transfer and flourishing evidence remain pending.

## Next decision

Use this screen outline and complete packet as the concrete Design review package. Retain the parent human gates and seek pending patron, librarian, service-owner and accessibility-practitioner review of relevance, authority, refusal, access, privacy and workload, preserving dissent and corrections. A subsequent Build may create a local rehearsal candidate for technical and interaction review; this brief grants no operational approval or pilot authorization. Expert draft for public deliberation in a rehearsal. No patron, librarian or practitioner has reviewed or approved it. Sequence 2 preserves the parent Understand, Map and Design artifacts as background, including their unresolved human gates and shared-device privacy requirements. Historical sequence labels inside that preserved material are not new evidence for this contribution.

The proposed task is to explore an invented community event, inspect an authored participation requirement and choose an acceptable next step. The people whose interests require review are adult patrons with varied reading, language and device access; librarians and volunteers who may provide assistance; and service owners who control actual event routes. None participate in this demonstration.

D1.problem challenge: difficulty with an account step may reflect an avoidable service requirement, unclear notice or unavailable route. The product must not treat independent online progress as the problem to solve. D5.context challenge: choosing help does not create staff capacity, language assistance, connectivity or time on a shared computer.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: patrons control whether to continue and may respond by selecting, pointing or speaking. Passing and declining require no justification. Librarians define what assistance can reasonably cover; service owners verify real routes before any later service use. Patron and practitioner review must examine whether the proposed task is wanted and understandable.

System requirements: keep preference separate from provision. For this rehearsal, show authored example conditions alongside each route and retain a visible statement that real availability is unknown. Choosing staff help changes the draft support request, not the staff availability state. Choosing paper opens complete invented materials, not a claim that the real service accepts paper.

Authority remains external to the candidate: it cannot register, reserve help, establish eligibility, verify accounts or determine capability. The candidate should use no open-text fields for this task; fixed choices can express its core decisions without inviting personal information.

## Experience and decisions

Opening mission: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Explore its example notice and decide what you would do next. This exercise cannot register anyone. Use only the fictional choices shown.” The small route board has text labels for Explore, Choose a route, Check a condition and Review your plan. Illustrations must carry no information absent from those labels.

Invented notice: “Community Drawing Hour offers a morning session and an afternoon session. Materials are provided in this example. The notice says: ‘Confirm your place.’ The route details below are invented for practice.” Session preference is optional and is not a booking.

Offer a local mock online route, asking staff to explain a step, a complete paper practice route, and pause/decline. Include “No route works for me” and “Leave undecided.” Reveal route details when selected. The online detail says: “This example portal requires an account step before confirmation. No account is created here.” Its controls are Inspect the requirement, Seek an explanation, Change route and Stop; it has no account, credential or contact fields.

The staff route says: “You would ask someone to explain the confirmation step. Real assistance and language support are unknown. No request is sent.” The paper route opens the packet below and says: “These are complete practice materials. Real paper acceptance is unknown.”

Record an initial draft using fixed choices. Invite, without requiring, one authored change: “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit.” If staff help was selected, retain that preference and visibly mark the dependency as unresolved. Offer wait without a promised time, inspect another route, remain undecided or stop. Never silently substitute an online route.

The final descriptive plan shows Before and Now: chosen route, explicit next action, who controls the relevant condition, support needed and fallback. Use “Not chosen” where a field is undecided. Every entry can be corrected; changing an entry replaces its dependent description. The result always says “Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.” No completion rating or ability judgment appears.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Origin: Public library access domain specialist, D1.problem; preserved dependency framing in sequence 2. Pair each route preference with its example condition and unresolved real provision. This prevents an interface choice from implying an available opportunity. Check by selecting staff help and applying the unavailable-staff condition: the preference remains, no assistance is confirmed, and reconsideration is possible without a deficit label.

R2 — Origin: Public library access domain specialist, D1.problem and D5.context; the seed’s unfamiliar-account condition. Keep the mock account step entirely descriptive and provide route reconsideration immediately. This lets a patron inspect a service barrier without disclosing information. Check every screen and state for absence of personal-data fields, account creation, external navigation and registration claims.

R3 — Origin: Public library access domain specialist, D5.context; sequence 2 preserves unknown language arrangements and assistance boundaries. Show “Language support: unknown” near the support decision. Use reviewed plain-language wording and text alternatives; do not invent available translations or interpreters. Permit oral or pointed responses during facilitated practice if a facilitator is actually available. Check that missing language support can leave the plan unresolved or stopped, without blocking access to paper materials. Patron review must determine appropriate language versions; plain English alone does not establish language access.

R4 — Origin: Public library access domain specialist, D5.context; sequence 2 preserves complete concealment, neutral focus and explicit clearing boundaries. Put Cover, Clear and Stop before task controls in keyboard order. Cover hides all route choices, descriptions and change messages from visual and assistive-technology access. Reveal and Resume are distinct actions. Clear removes the candidate-held draft and derived content, confirms that scope, and does not restart a paused or stopped exercise. Check these transitions from every task state, including clearing while covered. Inspect focus placement and magnified reflow. Device-wide removal must never be promised.

R5 — Origin: Public library access domain specialist, D1.problem and D5.context; sequence 2 preserves paper comparison and meaningful refusal. Make the packet below available without completing the digital journey. A patron can point, speak, mark, pass or stop. Check that the packet contains the task, requirement, change, correction and review prompts, and makes sense without interface instructions. Librarian review must examine printing, handling and facilitation effort.

R6 — Origin: Public library access domain specialist, D1.problem; the seed requests a second optional situation. Offer “Neighborhood Story Circle,” an invented event whose notice says “Check joining arrangements.” Present the same route choices with fewer suggestions, while retaining privacy, help, passing and correction. Any additional prompting must be recorded in later reviewed task evidence. Check that practice is optional and unlocks nothing; a changed plan cannot be presented as demonstrated transfer.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

The changed-condition design makes service dependency visible, but may add reading burden. Keep its initial wording short and reveal explanations on request. A complete paper route adds preparation and handling work, but provides a concrete non-AI comparison.

Retain the objection that clearer notices could solve the underlying problem more directly. Alternatives include the paper packet, conversation with available staff and revising service information before building a tool. Reviewers may prefer an alternative or reject the candidate.

Complete invented paper/facilitation packet:

Card A — Task and notice. “Community Drawing Hour is fictional. Choose a possible next step; you are not registering. Morning or afternoon sessions are offered in this example. Its notice says ‘Confirm your place.’ Pass, pause or stop at any time.”

Card B — Routes and conditions. “Online practice: the invented portal includes an account step; do not supply account information. Staff explanation: someone would explain the step if assistance were available; real availability and language support are unknown. Paper practice: use these cards; real acceptance of paper is unknown. You may also choose no workable route or remain undecided.”

Card C — Before plan. “Route: online / staff explanation / paper practice / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect the requirement / seek an explanation if support exists / examine another route / pause / stop / undecided. Support wanted: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none chosen. These choices describe a fictional preference, not available provision.” Marking is optional; pointing or speaking is sufficient.

Card D — Changed condition. “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Keep your preference, change it, leave it unresolved or stop. Waiting has no promised duration. No route becomes available merely because you choose it.”

Card E — Now plan and correction. Repeat Card C’s choices. Add “Control boundary: service owner controls the event requirement; library staff control assistance offered; you control whether to continue. Fallback: inspect another route / wait without a promised time / leave undecided / stop.” Correct by replacing a selection or asking the facilitator to restate it. Do not require a reason.

Card F — Privacy and facilitation. “Use fictional choices only. Folding or covering cards conceals them; it does not erase them. Agree how marked cards will be handled before practice. Stop or pass without explanation.” Facilitator script: “Would you like to point, speak, mark, pass or stop? What route, if any, would you choose? Here is the imagined change. Keep or change your choice? Shall I read your current plan so you can correct it?” Do not supply an answer, promise assistance or infer understanding. Facilitator availability itself remains a condition to establish.

Optional second card — “Neighborhood Story Circle is fictional. Its notice says ‘Check joining arrangements.’ Choose a route and a next action using Card C. Imagine your shared-computer time ends. Keep, revise, pause or stop. Review with Card E.” Offer further suggestions only on request; the paper option remains equally legitimate.

## Acceptance checks

Intended quality: an understandable, correctable route decision that preserves patron control and exposes service dependencies. Proposed checks in R1–R6 cover interaction behavior, privacy, language uncertainty and equivalent alternatives. None has been executed.

Technical verification must separately inspect keyboard order, visible focus, reflow, concealment, stale summaries, confirmed clearing and absence of network, storage and telemetry. Human interaction review must examine whether labels imply real provision, whether stopping is socially acceptable, and what assistance or reading burden the journey creates.

Review flourishing without equating task completion with success: agency includes refusal; dignity excludes deficit labels; access depends on actual conditions; belonging includes usable language arrangements; sustainable workload includes facilitation demand. Learning and transfer require separately reviewed evidence from a different task with support conditions documented.

## Evidence and unknowns

Sequence 2 is preserved parent context, not a participant observation or a technical finding. The seed supplies the fictional mission and restrictions. All requirements here are expert draft proposals. The unavailable-staff change is hypothetical, not a reported event.

Rival explanations for difficulty include ambiguous wording, language mismatch, inaccessible controls, interrupted device time and absent support. Apparent ease could reflect prior familiarity or facilitator prompting. Unknowns include demand for the tool, actual route options, staffing windows, language arrangements, paper acceptance, shared-device behavior and acceptable workload. Field evidence remains pending.

## Next decision

Expert draft for public deliberation in a rehearsal. No requirements here are approved. Sequence 2 preserves the parent Understand, Map and Design records and their unresolved human gates. It is a preservation event, not a new interaction finding. Sequence 5 supplies the current domain proposal, including the fictional event, separate preference and provision, complete paper materials and optional practice.

The task is to inspect the invented Community Drawing Hour notice, consider its authored confirmation requirement and choose an acceptable next step. Adult patrons, librarians, volunteers, service owners and accessibility practitioners have relevant interests; none participate in this demonstration.

D1.problem challenge: an unfamiliar account step may indicate unnecessary service friction, unclear information, language mismatch or unavailable support. More patron training is only one possible response and has no supporting evidence here. An acceptable outcome includes an unresolved plan, paper practice, seeking an explanation when assistance exists, or stopping.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: patrons retain authority over continuing and correcting their choices. Pointing, speaking, passing and declining remain legitimate. Available facilitators may read an authored notice or restate an explicit selection, but must not infer agreement, supply a preferred answer or promise assistance. Librarians and service owners must establish actual service conditions before any later operational use.

System requirements: distinguish the patron's preference, the fictional condition being explored, real provision that remains unknown, and the draft next action. Selecting staff help records a preference; it cannot create a staffed opportunity. Selecting paper practice opens complete invented materials; it cannot establish real paper acceptance. The mock online route may describe an account requirement but must contain no account or credential controls.

The coupling is conditional: a desired action may depend on understandable information, a usable route, device time and suitable assistance. The candidate can expose those dependencies and support reconsideration. It cannot supply missing service capacity. Authority over the event requirement belongs to the service owner; authority over offered assistance belongs to its provider; the patron controls participation in this exercise.

## Experience and decisions

Keep the primary journey short: explore the invented notice, choose a route, inspect one condition and review a draft. Use the four text-labelled route choices proposed in the seed: mock online practice, staff explanation, complete paper practice, and pause/decline. Also permit no workable route and undecided without requiring an explanation. Use fixed controls and no open-text fields for this candidate.

The first review describes the current choice. An optional explicit action, “Keep this as my initial plan,” records a temporary comparison snapshot. Without that action, show “Initial plan not recorded”; do not fabricate a baseline. Invite the authored change, “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit.” Keep the patron's preference and display its unresolved dependency. Offer reconsideration, waiting without a promised duration, remaining undecided or stopping. Never select another route automatically.

The current plan describes route, next action, control boundary, requested support and fallback. It always states “Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.” Changed fields receive descriptive feedback, such as “You changed from staff explanation to paper practice. Real paper acceptance is unknown.” Feedback must derive from explicit choices rather than judge progress.

The optional Neighborhood Story Circle task uses fewer suggestions and its own authored notice. Entering it requires a clear choice to replace the current task, with an opportunity to cancel. It unlocks nothing. Any apparent independence remains uninterpreted until reviewed evidence documents prior familiarity and support.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Dependency honesty. Origin: Systems engineer, D1.coupling; domain specialist at sequence 5; preserved Map dependency separation in sequence 2. Selecting a route must reveal its authored requirement, the party controlling it, real provision marked unknown and an action the patron can choose. Selecting staff explanation must leave staff availability unchanged. Acceptance check: select staff explanation, apply fictional unavailability and inspect the plan; the preference remains visible, the dependency becomes unresolved, no help is confirmed and every other route or refusal remains selectable. Context boundary: the changed condition is hypothetical and actual staffing is unknown.

R2 — Correctable comparison. Origin: Systems engineer, D4.verification; before/after proposal at sequence 5; sequence 2's temporary-memory and correction boundaries. Retain at most an explicitly recorded initial snapshot and the current draft within the active session. Generate descriptions from those selections; do not maintain an accumulating choice log. “Correct initial plan” must be distinct from “Change current plan,” with plain labels explaining which side changes. Acceptance check: record an initial staff preference, change the current route to paper, then correct the initial route to undecided. The comparison must describe those exact states and remove obsolete staff-derived claims. A cleared snapshot must never be reconstructed. Context boundary: before/after comparison is a design intention, not measured reflection or learning.

R3 — Separate privacy, activity and content. Origin: Systems engineer, D1.coupling and D4.verification; domain privacy requirement at sequence 5; preserved focus and concealment requirements in sequence 2. Place Cover, Clear and Stop before task controls in keyboard order. Cover hides every choice-bearing view, including both snapshots, feedback, optional practice and assistance descriptions, from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access. Focus moves to a neutral status. Reveal changes visibility only. Resume is an explicit separate action when activity is paused. Clear remains available while covered or stopped and removes all candidate-held selections and derived task content before confirming its limited scope. It preserves pause or stop and does not create a new draft. Acceptance check: exercise these transitions from an initial/current comparison, a changed-condition view and optional practice; verify neutral focus, no exposed choices while covered, no stale descriptions after clearing and no automatic restart. Context boundary: clearing the candidate does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.

R4 — Recovery without inferred intent. Origin: Systems engineer, D4.verification; sequence 2's interruption and loss boundaries; sequence 5's meaningful refusal. A fictional interruption pauses activity without changing route preference. Cancel closes a pending route change, task replacement or clear confirmation without modifying choices. If the page is reloaded, temporary task state is lost: the opening explains that no prior draft is restored and offers a fresh undecided task, paper materials or stopping. Acceptance check: cancel each pending action, interrupt a changed plan, then reload; unchanged choices survive cancellation, interruption does not silently resume, and reload restores no selections. Context boundary: no persistent storage or recovery history is permitted; these checks have not been executed.

R5 — Equivalent non-AI task and feasible support. Origin: Systems engineer, D1.problem and D1.coupling; domain packet at sequence 5; paper comparison and workload concerns preserved in sequence 2. Make the complete paper packet available before any digital choice. The packet must carry the same authored requirement, changed condition, initial/current choices, control boundary, correction and refusal. Oral assistance is conditional on an actually available person. Acceptance check: a reviewer can conduct the fictional decision using only the packet, without opening the digital route or supplying personal information; the facilitator can restate a corrected choice without selecting an answer. Context boundary: printing, physical access, language arrangements and handling effort need practitioner and affected-person review.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

The initial/current comparison makes a changed decision inspectable but adds state and wording. Keep it optional, retain only two temporary snapshots and show expanded explanations on request. Correctability matters more than filling every field.

Preserve dissent that a planning tool may be unnecessary. A clearer notice, verified route information or removal of a needless account step could address the barrier at its source. Complete paper practice and an ordinary conversation with available staff are non-AI options. None establishes operational service access.

Complete invented paper/facilitation packet for this state design:

Card A — Mission and notice. “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon sessions and says ‘Confirm your place.’ Choose a possible next step; you are not registering. Point, speak, mark, pass, pause or stop. Use no personal information.”

Card B — Route conditions. “Online practice: inspect an invented account requirement; do not create an account or supply details. Staff explanation: ask someone to explain a step if suitable assistance exists; real availability and language support are unknown. Paper practice: use these cards; real acceptance of paper is unknown. No workable route and undecided are valid choices.”

Card C — Initial plan, optional. “Route: online practice / staff explanation / paper practice / no workable route / undecided. Support wanted: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: examine another route / remain undecided / pause / stop.” Record only if wanted. No written reason is required.

Card D — Changed condition. “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Your preference does not make assistance available. Keep it unresolved, reconsider a route, wait without a promised duration, pause or stop.”

Card E — Current plan and correction. Repeat Card C's choices for the current plan. “The service owner controls the requirement; assistance providers control what help they offer; you control continuing. Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.” Correct the initial or current selection explicitly, or leave either blank. The facilitator restates the selected side and accepts correction without asking for justification.

Card F — Handling and facilitation. “Covering or folding cards conceals them; it does not erase them. Before marking, agree how cards will be handled. Stop or pass without explanation.” Facilitator script: “Would you like to point, speak, mark, pass or stop? Shall I read the notice? Which route, if any? Here is the imagined change. Keep or change your choice? Which plan should I correct?” Do not record personal information, infer understanding or promise service support.

Optional practice card — “Neighborhood Story Circle is invented. Its notice says ‘Check joining arrangements.’ Use Cards B, C and E to choose a next step. Imagine shared-computer time ends. Keep, revise, pause or stop.” Offer extra prompts only if requested; document their use in any later reviewed inquiry.

## Acceptance checks

Intended quality is an understandable, correctable decision with visible dependencies and legitimate refusal. R1–R5 define proposed behavioral checks. No check has been run and there is no observed implementation behavior.

Before interaction testing, technical verification must inspect keyboard order and focus, responsive reflow, concealment of every task-bearing component, stale summaries, cancellation, clearing while covered or stopped, and absence of network calls, persistent storage and telemetry. Demonstrating those behaviors would establish only the tested technical behavior.

Human review must separately examine whether the task is wanted, route labels imply provision, explanations impose excessive reading, privacy controls are discoverable and refusal feels legitimate. Patron, librarian and accessibility-practitioner review remains pending. Learning, transfer and flourishing require separate evidence and cannot be inferred from a changed plan, speed or completion.

## Evidence and unknowns

Evidence references are sequence 2's preserved context and sequence 5's domain draft. Neither supplies participant observations, approved requirements, technical results or field success. Historical sequence labels embedded in the parent are background and are not additional event citations here.

What changes after the proposed hypothetical challenge: staff preference persists while availability becomes unresolved; dependent descriptions update; reconsideration never substitutes a route automatically. The before/after proposal also requires bounded snapshots and complete clearing of both. These refine the current Design; they do not invalidate the earlier Map dependency account or require rerunning it.

Unknowns include demand for the tool, real event routes, account necessity, paper acceptance, staffing windows, language arrangements, device behavior and acceptable facilitation workload. Rival explanations for difficulty include service friction, unclear wording, inaccessible interaction and interrupted device time. Apparent ease could reflect familiarity or facilitator prompting. Field evidence remains pending.

Human-centered designer draft for public deliberation in a rehearsal. No patron, librarian, volunteer or practitioner has participated, approved these requirements or demonstrated their effectiveness. Sequence 2 preserves parent Understand, Map and Design context. Its embedded historical sequence labels are not additional evidence references. Sequences 5 and 7 supply the current domain and systems proposals.

The task is to explore the invented Community Drawing Hour, inspect an authored confirmation requirement and choose an acceptable next step. Relevant people include adult patrons with varied reading, language and device access; people providing assistance; and owners of service requirements. Participation may end with a choice, an unresolved condition, paper practice, passing or declining.

The discipline-specific challenge is that offering valid choices does not establish that people can understand, compare or exercise them with acceptable effort. A route board, support selector, initial snapshot, changed condition and final comparison could become a demanding exercise. A complete plan must not become the implied price of participation.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: patrons retain authority over whether to participate, what help they want and which explanation represents their choice. Selecting, pointing or speaking may express a choice; silence must not be interpreted as agreement. Passing requires no reason. An actually available facilitator may read authored information or restate selections, but must accept correction and avoid steering toward a preferred route.

Librarians and service owners must establish real routes, assistance boundaries and feasible support arrangements before operational use. Affected-person and accessibility-practitioner review must determine whether this task is wanted, its wording is understandable and its privacy controls are usable. These human gates remain unmet.

System requirements: present the mission and route choices with text alternatives, keep fictional conditions distinct from unknown real provision, and reveal detail without forcing additional decisions. Generate descriptions only from explicit selections. No personal fields, account controls, scoring, inferred understanding, storage, network activity or automatic service requests are permitted.

A patron controls continuing and changing a preference. Service owners control actual participation requirements. Assistance providers control what support they offer. Choosing help cannot change its availability. These authority boundaries must appear where the dependent decision occurs, not solely in Help.

## Experience and decisions

Opening mission: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Explore its example notice and choose a possible next step. This exercise cannot register anyone. Use fictional choices only.” The notice offers morning and afternoon sessions and says “Confirm your place.” Session preference is optional and must not resemble a reservation.

Use a small illustrated board with text labels: Explore the event, Choose a route, Check a condition, Review your plan. Illustrations provide orientation only. Do not require interaction with an illustration or completion of every step. Paper materials, Help, passing and stopping remain available from the opening.

The route decision offers mock online practice, staff explanation, paper practice and pause or decline, with equally reachable “No route works for me” and “Leave undecided.” No route is preselected. Selecting a route reveals one short consequence and its condition; it does not advance automatically. Longer explanation is available through “More detail,” which can be closed without changing choices or losing focus.

For online practice, show “This invented portal includes an account step. No account is created here.” Controls inspect the requirement, reconsider the route or stop; there are no account or contact fields. Staff explanation records a desired explanation and states that real assistance and language support are unknown. Paper practice opens complete fictional materials and states that real paper acceptance is unknown.

The patron may optionally keep the current selection as an initial plan. Skipping this leaves “Initial plan not recorded.” It does not block the changed condition, current plan or paper route. Support choices are optional and unselected by default; “None selected” does not mean no support is needed.

Offer the authored change: “Imagine staff are temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit.” Applying it preserves the selected route and marks its assistance dependency unresolved. Show options to keep the preference, reconsider, wait without a promised duration, leave undecided, pause or stop. Do not substitute an online route.

Review shows initial and current route, next action, support preference, control boundary and fallback using short labelled lines. “Fictional plan; no registration or request sent” remains adjacent to the output. “Correct initial plan” and “Change current plan” identify the side being edited. Cancellation preserves both sides. No reason for correction is requested.

Optional Neighborhood Story Circle practice uses fewer suggestions, but retains Help, paper, passing and correction. Choosing it clearly explains that it replaces the current task and offers cancellation. Requesting more support has no penalty and produces no capability label.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Limit entry burden. Origin: Human-centered designer, D2.prototyping and D5.context; route journey at sequence 5 and bounded comparison at sequence 7. Make the core task one route choice followed by inspection of its consequence. Session, support, initial snapshot and changed-condition practice remain optional. This supports participation without demanding a full planning worksheet. Acceptance check: a reviewer can inspect an online requirement and leave with an undecided next action without completing other selectors; no blocked control, missing-field message or completion judgment appears. Uncertainty: acceptable reading and interaction effort has not been established with patrons.

R2 — Preserve choice without steering. Origin: Human-centered designer, D3.agency; meaningful refusal at sequences 2 and 5. Put passing, undecided and no workable route alongside the decision, with comparable visual weight and neutral wording. Include “My next action is not listed” without requiring free text. Selecting it yields an unresolved description, not an inferred answer. Acceptance check: exercise each refusal path and inspect the output for unchanged authority, no justification prompt and no deficit label. Uncertainty: visible refusal may still feel socially difficult in facilitated use; affected-person review is required.

R3 — Keep dependency information local. Origin: Human-centered designer, D3.agency and D5.context; preference/provision separation at sequences 5 and 7. Show the fictional requirement, unknown real availability and controlling party near each route consequence. Keep these statements visible when longer detail is collapsed. Acceptance check: select staff explanation, apply fictional unavailability and close detail; preference remains visible, availability is unresolved and no staff request or assistance is confirmed. Context: this is an authored change, not an observed service incident.

R4 — Make representation correctable. Origin: Human-centered designer, D2.prototyping and D3.agency; snapshot rules at sequence 7. Use plain labels for initial and current plans, with distinct correction controls. Feedback describes only the changed selection and its dependency. Correction must replace dependent descriptions without retaining obsolete claims elsewhere. Acceptance check: record staff explanation, change the current route to paper, correct the initial route to undecided and cancel another edit. Both sides and all feedback must reflect precisely those explicit actions. Uncertainty: comprehension of two-plan comparison is untested; review may remove it while retaining a correctable current plan.

R5 — Support access without promising provision. Origin: Human-centered designer, D5.context; language and facilitation concerns at sequence 5. Use short text labels, meaningful text alternatives, visible keyboard focus and responsive reflow. Detail expansion returns focus to its trigger when closed; changing a selection must not move focus unexpectedly. Oral assistance is conditional on an available person. Language support remains unknown. Acceptance check: inspect the journey using keyboard operation, narrow layout, magnification and assistive technology; verify route labels, consequences and refusal remain reachable without illustration interpretation. These are proposed technical checks, not an accessibility certification. Patron review must determine wording and language arrangements.

R6 — Preserve privacy and stopping throughout. Origin: Human-centered designer, D2.prototyping and D3.agency; parent controls preserved at sequence 2 and state separation at sequence 7. Place Cover, Clear and Stop before task controls in keyboard order. Cover removes every choice-bearing view from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access and moves focus to neutral status. Reveal restores visibility only; paused or stopped activity requires explicit resumption. A clear confirmation must remain usable while covered and must not expose choices. Confirmed clearing removes initial/current plans and all derived messages, preserves paused or stopped activity and reports its limited scope. Cancellation preserves content. Acceptance check: exercise cover, reveal, cancel, confirmed clear and resume from comparison and optional-practice states; inspect focus and stale content. No check has been executed, and device-wide deletion cannot be claimed.

R7 — Keep practice and support voluntary. Origin: Human-centered designer, D3.agency and D5.context; optional second task at sequences 5 and 7. Practice unlocks nothing. Fewer suggestions must not remove Help or make support harder to request. A facilitator reads or restates only with permission and never treats silence as agreement. Acceptance check: skip practice, enter it, request detail, cancel replacement and stop; no reward, score or assertion of independence appears. Human review must examine prompting and facilitation effort. Learning or transfer cannot be inferred from these interactions.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Progressive detail reduces initial reading but can obscure conditions; therefore essential fiction, availability and control statements remain visible beside decisions. A before/after view makes changes inspectable but adds memory demands; it is optional and may be removed after review. Fixed choices limit personal-data solicitation but can miss an acceptable action; unlisted and undecided outcomes must remain valid.

Retain dissent that improving the service notice or removing an unnecessary account step could address the barrier more directly. Ordinary conversation with available staff and the complete paper packet below are non-AI options. Reviewers may choose an alternative or reject the candidate.

## Acceptance checks

Intended quality is a manageable, correctable decision that preserves participation authority and makes dependencies understandable. Requirements R1–R7 specify proposed observable checks; none has been performed. Intended quality must remain separate from observed technical behavior, which is currently absent.

Technical verification should inspect all reachable states for keyboard focus, text alternatives, reflow, cancellation, complete concealment, faithful summaries and confirmed clearing. It must also verify absence of network, storage, telemetry, personal fields and external navigation.

Affected-person and practitioner review must separately examine whether the task is wanted, whether refusal feels legitimate, which explanations are misunderstood and who bears reading or facilitation work. Do not treat speed, completion, a route change or reduced prompting as evidence of learning, transfer or flourishing.
