function derivePlan(d){
if(!d)return null;
let condition,authority;
if(d.route==='online'){
condition=d.task==='drawing'?'This invented portal has an account step before confirmation. No account is created here. Actual requirements and connectivity are unknown.':'Joining arrangements are unresolved in this example. No account requirement is stated. Actual arrangements and connectivity are unknown.';
authority='You control inspection and continuation. The service owner controls actual joining requirements.';
}else if(d.route==='staff'){
condition=d.context.staff?'In this example, staff are temporarily unavailable. The preference remains; an explanation is unresolved. Real availability and language support are unknown. No request is sent.':'The draft seeks an explanation if suitable assistance exists. Real availability and language support are unknown. No request is sent.';
authority='You choose whether to seek help. Assistance providers control what help they can offer; the service owner controls requirements.';
}else if(d.route==='paper'){
condition=d.context.packets?'In this example, prepared packets have run out. The materials can be viewed here, but a physical paper route is unresolved. No printing or replenishment is arranged.':'Physical paper use depends on a complete usable prepared packet actually being supplied. Viewing materials does not supply physical paper.';
condition+=' Real packet availability, usable format and service acceptance are unknown.';
authority='You control the medium preference. A materials provider controls physical supply; the service owner controls acceptance.';
}else{condition='No route commitment is implied. Actual routes, suitable assistance and material provision remain unknown.';authority='You control whether to continue, pass, reconsider or stop. Providers control support and materials; the service owner controls requirements.';}
let action=label(actions,d.action,'Undecided');
if(d.action==='inspect'&&d.task==='drawing')action='Inspect the invented account requirement';
if(d.action==='inspect'&&d.task==='story')action='Inspect the notice; joining arrangements remain unresolved';
if(d.action==='packet')action+='; possession, usable format and acceptance are unconfirmed'+(d.context.packets?' and fictional supply is exhausted':'');
if(d.action==='explain')action+='; no request sent'+(d.context.staff?' and fictional staff are unavailable':'');
if(d.task==='story'&&d.context.time)condition+=' Imagined shared-computer time ended; activity paused without replacing the preference.';
return {route:label(routes,d.route,'No route selected'),action,support:label(supports,d.support,'None selected')+(d.support?'':' — this does not mean no support is needed'),fallback:label(fallbacks,d.fallback,'None selected'),session:d.task==='drawing'?label(sessions,d.session,'None selected'):null,condition,authority,context:contextLabel(d)};
}
function transition(s,a){const n=clone(s);switch(a.type){
case 'cover': n.covered=!s.covered;if(n.covered&&n.activity==='active')n.activity='paused';n.clearConfirm=false;break;
case 'activity':n.activity=a.value;break;
case 'clearAsk':n.clearConfirm=true;break;
case 'clearCancel':n.clearConfirm=false;break;
case 'clear':n.draft=null;n.initial=null;n.editor=null;n.panel=null;n.compare=false;n.clearConfirm=false;n.switchTo=null;break;
case 'fresh':n.draft=makeDraft(a.task||'drawing');n.initial=null;n.editor=null;n.panel=null;n.compare=false;n.switchTo=null;break;
case 'route':if(n.draft){n.draft.route=a.value;n.draft.action='';}break;
case 'field':if(n.draft)n.draft[a.key]=a.value;break;
case 'condition':if(n.draft){n.draft.context[a.key]=!n.draft.context[a.key];if(a.key==='time'&&n.draft.context.time&&n.activity!=='stopped')n.activity='paused';}break;
case 'snapshot':if(n.draft&&!n.initial)n.initial=clone(n.draft);break;
case 'edit':{const d=a.side==='initial'?n.initial:n.draft;if(d){n.editor={side:a.side,draft:clone(d)};n.panel='editor';n.switchTo=null;}break;}
case 'editField':if(n.editor){n.editor.draft[a.key]=a.value;if(a.key==='route')n.editor.draft.action='';}break;
case 'commit':if(n.editor){const side=n.editor.side==='initial'?'initial':'draft';const prior=n[side];if(prior){n.editor.draft.context=clone(prior.context);n.editor.draft.task=prior.task;n[side]=clone(n.editor.draft);}n.editor=null;n.panel=null;}break;
case 'cancel':n.editor=null;n.panel=null;n.switchTo=null;break;
case 'panel':n.editor=null;n.switchTo=null;n.panel=a.value;break;
case 'compare':n.compare=!n.compare;break;
case 'switchAsk':n.editor=null;n.switchTo=a.task;n.panel='switch';break;
case 'switch':if(n.switchTo){n.draft=makeDraft(n.switchTo);n.initial=null;n.editor=null;n.panel=null;n.compare=false;n.switchTo=null;}break;
}return n;}

## Problem and people
Adult patrons explore an invented community event and choose an acceptable next step. Independent online completion is not the objective. Reference: complete revised Design, sequence 20; Map is preserved as background at sequence 2, but its full text is not supplied here. No participant observations or approvals exist.

## Human and system capability
Patrons retain participation and representation authority. Providers control assistance and physical supply; service owners control actual requirements. The candidate separates these dependencies, describes explicit choices and collects no personal information. Actual formats, language support and capacity remain unknown.

## Experience and decisions
The supplied source implements Drawing Hour notice inspection, route choices, an invented account condition and optional staff/supply changes. Choices visibly alter descriptive consequences. Initial/current comparison and correction are optional; cancel preserves committed choices. Story Circle has separate unresolved arrangements and a device-time pause. No critical missing requirement was identified in source review.

## Requirements and rationale
Domain and Systems drafts (5, 7; D1.problem/D1.coupling/D5.context) require preference to remain distinct from provision: exercise staff unavailability and paper exhaustion. Designer and Learning drafts (9, 11; D2.practice/D2.prototyping/D4.transfer) require low-burden inspection without completion judgments: inspect, leave undecided and stop; check Story Circle for condition leakage. Responsible AI draft (13; D3.agency/D3.delegation/D5.privacy) requires faithful correction and shared-device control: exercise both editors, cancel, cover, reveal, resume and confirmed clearing. These are acceptance checks, not observed browser results.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives
Optional comparison adds reflection opportunities and exposure burden. Fixed choices reduce disclosure but omit intentions; unlisted, unworkable and undecided choices retain dissent. Complete paper/facilitation cards provide a non-AI preparation route, conditional on independent physical provision. Sequence 18's hypothetical supply failure is retained: screen viewing never resolves exhausted supplies or replaces paper preference. Clearer service information remains a rival intervention.

## Acceptance checks
Sequence 32 reports the sequence 29 wording correction, a syntax pass and seven offline check groups. Their report is bounded technical evidence; this turn executes no checks. Next exercise keyboard/focus recovery, assistive-technology announcements, narrow and magnified layouts, correction/cancellation, task replacement, cover/resume and clearing from pending-edit states. Separately provide the actual complete packet and inspect screen-independent use. Browser, accessibility, physical delivery and human checks remain pending.

## Evidence and unknowns
Review basis: revised Design 20, specialist drafts 5/7/9/11/13, hypothetical event 18, correction request 29 and implementation 32. Field, learning, retention, transfer and flourishing evidence are pending.

This acceptance grants no operational approval, field release or efficacy claim.","revision":1,"trigger_seq":34},"design":{"body":"## Problem and people

Access Studio: choose a route, keep control is a fictional community-event participation exercise. The task is to explore an invented notice, inspect a participation condition and choose an acceptable next step. Independent online completion is not the objective. An unresolved choice, conditional assistance, paper preference, passing or stopping is legitimate.

Relevant people are adult patrons with varied reading, languages and device access; librarians, volunteers, service owners and accessibility practitioners. None participates in this rehearsal. This is a provisional Design revision, not an approved requirement set.

Sequence 18 supplies one hypothetical event: prepared packets run out, and a fictional patron objects that viewing cards on a screen does not provide the desired paper route. This is authored scenario data, not a participant quotation or service incident. It invalidates the delivery-equivalence wording in sequence 15. Revise Design only: the Understand framing and Map separation of preference from provision remain applicable, with their human gates unresolved. Sequence 2 records parent preservation, not successful verification.

Rival explanations for difficulty include unclear notices, unnecessary account requirements, language or format mismatch, inaccessible controls, interrupted device time and absent assistance. Rejecting a medium may express ordinary preference. Apparent ease could reflect familiarity, repeated controls or facilitator prompting. Neither pattern establishes a learning need.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: patrons control participation, support preferences and whether a description represents their choices. Selecting, pointing or speaking may express a decision; silence is not agreement. Passing and stopping require no explanation. An actually available facilitator may read authored information or restate selections with permission, but may not select an answer, infer understanding or promise service assistance.

Service owners control actual participation requirements and accepted routes. Assistance providers control offered support. An accountable materials provider must establish complete usable packets independently of the candidate before offering a facilitated paper exercise. Librarians must examine preparation, supply, formats, language arrangements, shared-device handling and workload. No provider, supplies or support capacity is presumed available.

System requirements: distinguish explicit preference, authored example conditions, unknown real provision and next action. For paper, separately represent content available to view, fictional physical supply, unknown real packet availability, usable format and service acceptance. Fixed local rules suffice; no AI inference is needed. The candidate cannot register, send requests, create accounts, arrange printing, replenish supplies, determine eligibility or judge capability.

Use no personal, credential or account fields, open text, scores, deficit labels, network, storage, telemetry, external assets, links or real submissions. Keep only the current draft, optional initial snapshot and temporary editing/activity state. A choice cannot create staff capacity, a physical packet or acceptance by a service.

## Experience and decisions

Opening mission: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Explore its example notice and choose a possible next step. This exercise cannot register anyone. Use fictional choices only.” The invented notice offers morning and afternoon sessions, says materials are provided in this example and asks patrons to “Confirm your place.” Session preference is optional and never a reservation.

A small illustrated route board has complete text labels: Explore the event, Choose a route, Check a condition, Review your plan. Illustration conveys no additional required information. One route choice reveals its consequence without automatic advancement. No completed worksheet, baseline or second task is required.

Offer mock online practice, conditional staff explanation and a paper preference, alongside No route works for me and Leave undecided. Pause, Decline and Stop remain equally reachable activity choices. No route is preselected. Longer detail is optional; essential fiction, provision and control statements stay visible when detail is closed.

Online practice reveals: “This invented portal includes an account step before confirmation. No account is created here.” Local controls inspect that requirement, seek an explanation if assistance exists, reconsider or stop. Staff explanation yields: “Your draft seeks an explanation if suitable assistance exists. Real availability and language support are unknown. No request is sent.” Neither route contains account or contact fields.

Paper preference reveals two distinct actions. “View the paper materials” opens the complete authored packet without changing the chosen route or its delivery condition. “Use a prepared paper packet” expresses a preferred next action conditional on a complete usable packet actually being supplied. It does not confirm possession, create a packet or start a service process. Show beside both: “Real packet availability, usable format and service acceptance are unknown. Viewing these materials does not provide physical paper.” Viewing is optional; a person rejecting the screen need not inspect it.

Offer optional authored changes through short controls, without requiring every scenario. The existing change imagines staff temporarily unavailable. The new change from sequence 18 imagines prepared packets exhausted. Its paper consequence reads: “In this example, prepared packets have run out. The materials can be viewed here, but a physical paper route is unresolved. No printing or replenishment is arranged.” Preserve paper preference and offer keeping it unresolved, another route, undecided, pause or stop. Never substitute screen practice. Neither hypothetical condition changes unknown real provision.

The current plan is always reviewable. Optional “Keep this as my initial plan” captures explicit choices and their condition context; otherwise show “Initial plan not recorded.” Support and fallback are optional. “None selected” never means “No support needed.” Output describes route, next action, support preference, delivery/assistance dependencies, controlling party and fallback. Keep “Fictional plan; no registration or request sent” adjacent to it.

Before/Now comparison is optional. “Correct initial plan” edits initial choices within their original condition context; “Change current plan” edits current choices. Identify the side being edited. Commit replaces dependent wording; Cancel preserves committed state. Viewing materials cannot remove an exhausted-supply condition, fabricate a baseline or rewrite the initial context. Feedback describes selections and unresolved conditions without praise, recommendations or capability judgments.

Optional Neighborhood Story Circle has its own notice: “Check joining arrangements.” Arrangements remain unresolved; no account requirement is stated. Its authored change imagines shared-computer time ending, which pauses activity without changing preference. Use fewer initial suggestions while retaining Help, paper content, correction, refusal and stopping. Task replacement explains removal of the previous draft and offers Cancel. No Drawing Hour condition is silently inherited.

Cover, Clear and Stop precede task controls in keyboard order. Cover conceals all choice-bearing content, pending edits and announcements, moves focus to neutral status and pauses active practice; stopped practice stays stopped. Reveal changes visibility only. Resume is separate. Confirmed Clear removes task choices, snapshots, scenario selections, pending edits and derived messages, preserves visibility/activity status and creates no new draft. Cancel clearing preserves content. A fresh undecided draft requires explicit action. Reload restores no prior choices. Clearing concerns candidate-held content, not device-wide records.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Honest dependencies and authority. Origins: Public library specialist, sequence 5, D1.problem/D5.context; Systems engineer, sequence 7, D1.coupling; Responsible AI specialist, sequence 13, D3.delegation. Pair each preference with its authored condition, controlling party and unknown real provision. Human reason: a preference is not another party’s commitment. System reason: route selection must not alter assistance or material availability. Check: choose staff explanation and apply fictional unavailability; preference persists, assistance is unresolved, no request is confirmed and alternatives remain reachable. Actual provision is unknown.

R2 — Physical paper delivery. Origins: integrated R7 at sequence 15 and scenario at sequence 18, D1.coupling/D3.agency/D4.verification; paper proposals at sequences 5 and 7. Separate viewing content from intending to use independently prepared paper. Human reason: choosing paper does not imply acceptance of screen use. System reason: content visibility cannot satisfy delivery. Check: choose paper, record an initial plan if wanted, apply exhausted supplies and view the packet; preference persists, physical provision stays unresolved and no printing or replacement medium is promised. Separately give a reviewer the actual complete packet to conduct the task without a screen. Without that packet, the delivery check is unmet. Usable formats and human readiness remain pending.

R3 — Manageable practice and descriptive feedback. Origins: Human-centered designer, sequence 9, D2.prototyping/D5.context; Learning scientist, sequence 11, D2.practice. One choice reveals a concrete consequence; all additional selectors, snapshots and changes remain optional. Human reason: participation must not require a finished plan. System reason: inspection is a coherent task without mandatory collection. Check: inspect the account condition, leave the next action undecided and stop without validation errors or completion judgments. Patron review must establish acceptable burden and wording.

R4 — Contestable synthesis and faithful correction. Origins: Systems engineer, sequence 7, D4.verification; designer, sequence 9, D3.agency; Responsible AI specialist, sequence 13, D3.delegation; scenario, sequence 18. Derive each plan from explicit choices and its own condition context, with separate initial/current correction and cancellation. Human reason: readable output must remain rejectable. System reason: edits must remove stale dependent claims without accumulating history. Check: record paper before supply exhaustion, apply exhaustion, change current route, correct the initial preference to undecided and cancel another edit. Each side must retain its own conditions and exact committed choices; viewing content must not repair supply. Comparison comprehension is untested.

R5 — Access, privacy and recovery. Origins: Systems engineer, sequence 7, D1.coupling/D4.verification; designer, sequence 9, D2.prototyping/D5.context; Responsible AI specialist, sequence 13, D5.privacy; preserved controls at sequence 2. Provide plain labels, text alternatives, responsive reflow, visible focus and predictable focus restoration. Separate visibility, activity and content presence. Human reason: interruption must preserve exposure and continuation control. System reason: hiding one summary cannot conceal every representation. Check cover/reveal/resume, cancel/clear, stopping and reload from comparison, supply-change and practice states; inspect keyboard and assistive-technology access, announcements and stale content. Also inspect absence of prohibited data collection, storage and external activity. No checks or accessibility certification exist.

R6 — Practice and evidence boundaries. Origins: Learning scientist, sequence 11, D4.evidence/D4.transfer; practice proposals at sequences 5, 7 and 9. Story Circle has its own unresolved notice and device-time change; help remains reachable. Human reason: immediate supported performance is not demonstrated transfer. System reason: task-specific data and conditions must not leak across replacement. Check entry, requested detail, cancellation, unresolved arrangements and stopping; no inherited account requirement, reward, score or independence claim appears. Later retention/adaptation requires a separate reviewed task, timing and documented support conditions.

R7 — Human readiness and alternatives. Origins: domain specialist, sequence 5, D5.context; Responsible AI specialist, sequence 13, D3.delegation/D5.privacy; scenario, sequence 18. Make complete packet content inspectable before digital participation, but describe screen-independent use only as conditional on separate provision. Human reason: refusal, format choice and support demand require accountable arrangements. System reason: the candidate cannot approve readiness. Check that reviewers can distinguish preference, viewing and physical use; a prepared packet must support the full decision without the screen. Patron, librarian, service-owner and practitioner review must establish relevance, handling, formats and sustainable workload before later use. No operational approval is supplied.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Local dependency statements add reading but prevent hidden assumptions. Progressive detail may reduce burden while obscuring conditions, so essential limits stay visible. Optional comparison enables inspectable revision but adds state, privacy exposure and memory demands; review may remove it. Fixed choices avoid personal disclosure but omit possibilities, so unlisted and undecided outcomes remain valid.

Retain dissent: clearer notices, verified route information or removal of unnecessary account friction may solve the problem directly. A separately prepared static route board and packet are non-AI options. Conversation depends on an actually available person. Reviewers may choose these alternatives or stop development. Digital packet inspection alone is not equivalent offline delivery.

Complete invented paper/facilitation packet, to be independently prepared if paper practice is offered:

Card A — Notice and mission. “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Morning and afternoon sessions are offered; materials are provided in this example. Its notice says ‘Confirm your place.’ Explore a possible next step; nobody is registered. Use no personal information. Point, speak, mark, pass, pause or stop. Session preference: morning / afternoon / undecided; optional.”

Card B — Routes and authority. “Online practice describes an invented account step before confirmation; create no account and provide no details. Staff explanation depends on suitable assistance; real availability and language support are unknown. Paper practice depends on a complete usable prepared packet; real availability, format and service acceptance are unknown. Viewing content on a screen does not supply paper. No workable route and undecided are valid. You control continuing; the service owner controls requirements; providers control help and materials.”

Card C — Optional initial plan. “Route: online / staff explanation / paper preference / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect requirement / seek explanation if assistance exists / use a prepared packet if supplied / examine another route / wait without a promised duration / action not listed / undecided. Support preference: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: another route / undecided / pause / stop. Condition context: no hypothetical change / staff unavailable / packets exhausted / both.” Mark only if wanted. None selected does not establish no support needed.

Card D — Optional changes. “Imagine staff temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Your preference cannot make assistance available. Imagine prepared packets have run out. Viewing materials does not supply a physical packet; no printing or replenishment is arranged.” Choose either imagined condition, both or neither. Keep the preference unresolved, reconsider, wait without a promised duration, leave undecided, pause or stop. These are hypothetical changes, not reports.

Card E — Current plan. “Route: online / staff explanation / paper preference / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect requirement / seek explanation if assistance exists / use a prepared packet if supplied / examine another route / wait without a promised duration / action not listed / undecided. Support preference: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: another route / undecided / pause / stop. Condition context: no hypothetical change / staff unavailable / packets exhausted / both. Physical supply, usable format and acceptance remain separate questions. Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.”

Card F — Correction, handling and facilitation. “Identify initial or current; replace the chosen mark or ask for a restatement. Initial choices retain their original condition context. An unrecorded initial plan stays unrecorded. Cancel leaves committed marks unchanged; no reason or score is required. Before marking, agree who may see the cards and how they will be handled. Unmarked participation is valid. Folding conceals; it does not erase.” Facilitator script: “Would you like to point, speak, mark, pass or stop? May I read the notice? Which route, if any? Would you like an imagined change? May I restate your choice so you can correct it?” Await explicit permission; collect no personal details, select no preferred answer and promise no provision.

Optional Story Circle card — “Neighborhood Story Circle is invented. Its notice says ‘Check joining arrangements’; arrangements remain unresolved and no account requirement is stated. Choose online notice inspection, conditional staff explanation, paper preference, no workable route or undecided. Use Cards C and E for choices, leaving Drawing Hour changes unused. Imagine shared-computer time ends; pause without replacing your preference. Correct, request detail, pass or stop. This is optional practice, not evidence of learning or transfer.”

Preparation note — Having this text does not establish physical supplies. Before offering paper practice, a human provider must prepare and inspect complete usable materials and handling arrangements. For the exhausted-supply scenario, use a separately prepared scenario card or oral delivery with an available facilitator; do not pretend the absent packet has been supplied.

## Acceptance checks

R1–R7 define proposed observable checks; none has run. Intended quality is a voluntary, manageable and correctable decision with honest dependencies. No implemented candidate or observed technical behavior is supplied here.

Technical verification must exercise correction, cancellation, replacement, concealment, clearing and reload, including focus, announcements and narrow/magnified layouts. Physical delivery verification separately requires the prepared packet; screen inspection cannot pass it. Passing any check establishes only the exercised behavior.

Human interaction review must examine wantedness, comprehension, refusal, language/format arrangements, privacy discoverability and provider burden. Learning, retention, transfer and flourishing require separate inquiry. Completion, speed, route revision or fewer prompts establish none of them.

## Evidence and unknowns

Sequence 15 supplies the integrated Design and its specialist lineage at sequences 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. Sequence 18 is the hypothetical review trigger. Sequence 2 preserves immutable parent context. These are draft and scenario evidence, not observations, approvals or executed checks.

Changed after sequence 18: paper viewing no longer implies screen-independent delivery; paper preference survives exhausted fictional supplies; initial/current plans retain supply context; human preparation and a separate physical-delivery check are explicit. Existing staff-dependency, correction, privacy and practice boundaries remain.

Unknowns include demand, actual routes, account necessity, packet supply and replenishment, usable formats, language arrangements, assistance, shared-device behavior and sustainable workload. Agency, dignity, access and belonging depend on actual participation conditions. Field pilot, learning, transfer and flourishing evidence remain pending.

## Next decision

Replace sequence 15’s Design brief with this bounded revision in response to sequence 18; do not rerun Understand or Map. Next, prepare paired screen-outline and independently provisioned packet review materials for pending patron, librarian, service-owner and accessibility-practitioner review. Preserve objections and corrections. Review may simplify comparison, select a non-AI service improvement, permit candidate development or stop. rejected_response.artifact_body:
Review basis and scope. Revised Design 20 responded to hypothetical supply failure 18 by separating paper viewing from physical provision. Build 32 reported earlier implementation checks; those reports are not additional browser observations. Event 38 is actual host technical evidence for artifact 35, with matching artifact/build hash eacb040c511d572b19b34572920944b0fffe55fcb01026f01dc29e9af1af4cfb. The immutable parent at 2 remains background. This iteration requested Design and Build before technical review; it did not rerun Instrument/Deploy or conduct a pilot. The packet supplies evidence, not authorization.

Evidence classes. Event 38 independently reports corrected-source syntax, focused Node helper, integration and packaging passes. The helper exercised offline stub/pure-state behavior; these passes do not establish browser interaction or scientific validity. Separately, the hosted browser exercised fictional choices at 1280 × 720 on macOS. It observed distinct routes, unresolved staff and paper dependencies, separate initial/current condition contexts, current-editor cancellation and support commitment, cover/reveal/resume, rendered packet and Help, replacement and Story Circle isolation, confirmed clearing and reload. Limited interface observations were first-Tab access to Cover, absent open-text/password/email fields, no horizontal overflow at that viewport and no recorded console errors. None establishes comprehensive accessibility, privacy or responsive conformance.

Concrete acceptance ledger. Retain R1/R2: selecting staff or paper and applying an authored shortage must preserve preference and unresolved provision; viewing materials must not repair supply. Event 38 supports these exercised interactions. Physical acceptance separately requires a complete usable packet supplied to a reviewer who can inspect the notice, choose, encounter a changed condition, correct and stop without a screen; delivery and print layout remain untested.

Retain R3/R4: inspection may end undecided or stopped, and each editor must describe only its committed choices and own condition context. Event 38 supports the exercised current-editor cancellation, support commitment and comparison contexts. It does not report exercising initial-plan correction, every dependent-wording change or every pending-edit recovery. Acceptance requires correcting both sides, cancelling each and checking that stale claims disappear without rewriting the other side or fabricating an initial plan.

Retain R5/R6: cover must conceal all choice-bearing representations, reveal must leave activity paused, resume must be explicit, and confirmed clear must remove plans and pending state without creating a draft. Event 38 supports the reported paths, replacement cancellation, task isolation and reload. Extend review to both editors, pending confirmations, announcements, full keyboard operation, focus restoration, magnification, narrow layouts and assistive technology. Verify no prohibited network, storage, telemetry or external actions directly; absent rendered fields and helper passes alone are insufficient. Story Circle's unresolved arrangements and device-time pause were observed, but supported practice is not transfer evidence.

Human evidence still needed. R7 requires affected-person, librarian, service-owner and accessibility-practitioner review through accountable human gates; none has occurred. With separately authorized inquiry, examine whether participants can explain or correct the plan in their chosen mode, find refusal and clearing, distinguish preference from provision, and express that no route works. Include varied reading, language, device and access circumstances without deficit labels or patron scoring. Document missing coverage and support conditions rather than generalizing from the assistant's walkthrough. Examine actual assistance and materials workload separately from patron interaction.

Comparison and causal limits. Before/Now records authored choices within an exercise; it is not a measured baseline or treatment comparison. Familiarity, repeated controls, prompting, language/format mismatch, account friction and absent provision remain rival explanations. Compare the candidate with clearer notices and a complete static paper route under documented conditions before attributing benefit to the interface. Route revision, speed, completion and fewer prompts cannot establish capability gains. Learning would require reviewed task evidence over time; transfer would require a distinct task and context with support conditions documented. No retention, field, service-readiness or flourishing outcomes exist.

Retained dissent and next decision. The supply challenge changed delivery wording and acceptance boundaries: screen viewing no longer counts as paper provision, and shortage remains unresolved. Keep passing, oral assistance when available, paper, undecided and stopping legitimate. Accept only the reported technical behaviors as evidence for continued review. Human reviewers may simplify comparison, prefer the independently provisioned non-AI packet or service-information improvement, or stop. No human approval, operational release or efficacy claim is supplied.

This acceptance grants no operational approval, field release or efficacy claim.","revision":1,"trigger_seq":34},"design":{"body":"## Problem and people

Access Studio: choose a route, keep control is a fictional community-event participation exercise. The task is to explore an invented notice, inspect a participation condition and choose an acceptable next step. Independent online completion is not the objective. An unresolved choice, conditional assistance, paper preference, passing or stopping is legitimate.

Relevant people are adult patrons with varied reading, languages and device access; librarians, volunteers, service owners and accessibility practitioners. None participates in this rehearsal. This is a provisional Design revision, not an approved requirement set.

Sequence 18 supplies one hypothetical event: prepared packets run out, and a fictional patron objects that viewing cards on a screen does not provide the desired paper route. This is authored scenario data, not a participant quotation or service incident. It invalidates the delivery-equivalence wording in sequence 15. Revise Design only: the Understand framing and Map separation of preference from provision remain applicable, with their human gates unresolved. Sequence 2 records parent preservation, not successful verification.

Rival explanations for difficulty include unclear notices, unnecessary account requirements, language or format mismatch, inaccessible controls, interrupted device time and absent assistance. Rejecting a medium may express ordinary preference. Apparent ease could reflect familiarity, repeated controls or facilitator prompting. Neither pattern establishes a learning need.

## Human and system capability

Human requirements: patrons control participation, support preferences and whether a description represents their choices. Selecting, pointing or speaking may express a decision; silence is not agreement. Passing and stopping require no explanation. An actually available facilitator may read authored information or restate selections with permission, but may not select an answer, infer understanding or promise service assistance.

Service owners control actual participation requirements and accepted routes. Assistance providers control offered support. An accountable materials provider must establish complete usable packets independently of the candidate before offering a facilitated paper exercise. Librarians must examine preparation, supply, formats, language arrangements, shared-device handling and workload. No provider, supplies or support capacity is presumed available.

System requirements: distinguish explicit preference, authored example conditions, unknown real provision and next action. For paper, separately represent content available to view, fictional physical supply, unknown real packet availability, usable format and service acceptance. Fixed local rules suffice; no AI inference is needed. The candidate cannot register, send requests, create accounts, arrange printing, replenish supplies, determine eligibility or judge capability.

Use no personal, credential or account fields, open text, scores, deficit labels, network, storage, telemetry, external assets, links or real submissions. Keep only the current draft, optional initial snapshot and temporary editing/activity state. A choice cannot create staff capacity, a physical packet or acceptance by a service.

## Experience and decisions

Opening mission: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Explore its example notice and choose a possible next step. This exercise cannot register anyone. Use fictional choices only.” The invented notice offers morning and afternoon sessions, says materials are provided in this example and asks patrons to “Confirm your place.” Session preference is optional and never a reservation.

A small illustrated route board has complete text labels: Explore the event, Choose a route, Check a condition, Review your plan. Illustration conveys no additional required information. One route choice reveals its consequence without automatic advancement. No completed worksheet, baseline or second task is required.

Offer mock online practice, conditional staff explanation and a paper preference, alongside No route works for me and Leave undecided. Pause, Decline and Stop remain equally reachable activity choices. No route is preselected. Longer detail is optional; essential fiction, provision and control statements stay visible when detail is closed.

Online practice reveals: “This invented portal includes an account step before confirmation. No account is created here.” Local controls inspect that requirement, seek an explanation if assistance exists, reconsider or stop. Staff explanation yields: “Your draft seeks an explanation if suitable assistance exists. Real availability and language support are unknown. No request is sent.” Neither route contains account or contact fields.

Paper preference reveals two distinct actions. “View the paper materials” opens the complete authored packet without changing the chosen route or its delivery condition. “Use a prepared paper packet” expresses a preferred next action conditional on a complete usable packet actually being supplied. It does not confirm possession, create a packet or start a service process. Show beside both: “Real packet availability, usable format and service acceptance are unknown. Viewing these materials does not provide physical paper.” Viewing is optional; a person rejecting the screen need not inspect it.

Offer optional authored changes through short controls, without requiring every scenario. The existing change imagines staff temporarily unavailable. The new change from sequence 18 imagines prepared packets exhausted. Its paper consequence reads: “In this example, prepared packets have run out. The materials can be viewed here, but a physical paper route is unresolved. No printing or replenishment is arranged.” Preserve paper preference and offer keeping it unresolved, another route, undecided, pause or stop. Never substitute screen practice. Neither hypothetical condition changes unknown real provision.

The current plan is always reviewable. Optional “Keep this as my initial plan” captures explicit choices and their condition context; otherwise show “Initial plan not recorded.” Support and fallback are optional. “None selected” never means “No support needed.” Output describes route, next action, support preference, delivery/assistance dependencies, controlling party and fallback. Keep “Fictional plan; no registration or request sent” adjacent to it.

Before/Now comparison is optional. “Correct initial plan” edits initial choices within their original condition context; “Change current plan” edits current choices. Identify the side being edited. Commit replaces dependent wording; Cancel preserves committed state. Viewing materials cannot remove an exhausted-supply condition, fabricate a baseline or rewrite the initial context. Feedback describes selections and unresolved conditions without praise, recommendations or capability judgments.

Optional Neighborhood Story Circle has its own notice: “Check joining arrangements.” Arrangements remain unresolved; no account requirement is stated. Its authored change imagines shared-computer time ending, which pauses activity without changing preference. Use fewer initial suggestions while retaining Help, paper content, correction, refusal and stopping. Task replacement explains removal of the previous draft and offers Cancel. No Drawing Hour condition is silently inherited.

Cover, Clear and Stop precede task controls in keyboard order. Cover conceals all choice-bearing content, pending edits and announcements, moves focus to neutral status and pauses active practice; stopped practice stays stopped. Reveal changes visibility only. Resume is separate. Confirmed Clear removes task choices, snapshots, scenario selections, pending edits and derived messages, preserves visibility/activity status and creates no new draft. Cancel clearing preserves content. A fresh undecided draft requires explicit action. Reload restores no prior choices. Clearing concerns candidate-held content, not device-wide records.

## Requirements and rationale

R1 — Honest dependencies and authority. Origins: Public library specialist, sequence 5, D1.problem/D5.context; Systems engineer, sequence 7, D1.coupling; Responsible AI specialist, sequence 13, D3.delegation. Pair each preference with its authored condition, controlling party and unknown real provision. Human reason: a preference is not another party’s commitment. System reason: route selection must not alter assistance or material availability. Check: choose staff explanation and apply fictional unavailability; preference persists, assistance is unresolved, no request is confirmed and alternatives remain reachable. Actual provision is unknown.

R2 — Physical paper delivery. Origins: integrated R7 at sequence 15 and scenario at sequence 18, D1.coupling/D3.agency/D4.verification; paper proposals at sequences 5 and 7. Separate viewing content from intending to use independently prepared paper. Human reason: choosing paper does not imply acceptance of screen use. System reason: content visibility cannot satisfy delivery. Check: choose paper, record an initial plan if wanted, apply exhausted supplies and view the packet; preference persists, physical provision stays unresolved and no printing or replacement medium is promised. Separately give a reviewer the actual complete packet to conduct the task without a screen. Without that packet, the delivery check is unmet. Usable formats and human readiness remain pending.

R3 — Manageable practice and descriptive feedback. Origins: Human-centered designer, sequence 9, D2.prototyping/D5.context; Learning scientist, sequence 11, D2.practice. One choice reveals a concrete consequence; all additional selectors, snapshots and changes remain optional. Human reason: participation must not require a finished plan. System reason: inspection is a coherent task without mandatory collection. Check: inspect the account condition, leave the next action undecided and stop without validation errors or completion judgments. Patron review must establish acceptable burden and wording.

R4 — Contestable synthesis and faithful correction. Origins: Systems engineer, sequence 7, D4.verification; designer, sequence 9, D3.agency; Responsible AI specialist, sequence 13, D3.delegation; scenario, sequence 18. Derive each plan from explicit choices and its own condition context, with separate initial/current correction and cancellation. Human reason: readable output must remain rejectable. System reason: edits must remove stale dependent claims without accumulating history. Check: record paper before supply exhaustion, apply exhaustion, change current route, correct the initial preference to undecided and cancel another edit. Each side must retain its own conditions and exact committed choices; viewing content must not repair supply. Comparison comprehension is untested.

R5 — Access, privacy and recovery. Origins: Systems engineer, sequence 7, D1.coupling/D4.verification; designer, sequence 9, D2.prototyping/D5.context; Responsible AI specialist, sequence 13, D5.privacy; preserved controls at sequence 2. Provide plain labels, text alternatives, responsive reflow, visible focus and predictable focus restoration. Separate visibility, activity and content presence. Human reason: interruption must preserve exposure and continuation control. System reason: hiding one summary cannot conceal every representation. Check cover/reveal/resume, cancel/clear, stopping and reload from comparison, supply-change and practice states; inspect keyboard and assistive-technology access, announcements and stale content. Also inspect absence of prohibited data collection, storage and external activity. No checks or accessibility certification exist.

R6 — Practice and evidence boundaries. Origins: Learning scientist, sequence 11, D4.evidence/D4.transfer; practice proposals at sequences 5, 7 and 9. Story Circle has its own unresolved notice and device-time change; help remains reachable. Human reason: immediate supported performance is not demonstrated transfer. System reason: task-specific data and conditions must not leak across replacement. Check entry, requested detail, cancellation, unresolved arrangements and stopping; no inherited account requirement, reward, score or independence claim appears. Later retention/adaptation requires a separate reviewed task, timing and documented support conditions.

R7 — Human readiness and alternatives. Origins: domain specialist, sequence 5, D5.context; Responsible AI specialist, sequence 13, D3.delegation/D5.privacy; scenario, sequence 18. Make complete packet content inspectable before digital participation, but describe screen-independent use only as conditional on separate provision. Human reason: refusal, format choice and support demand require accountable arrangements. System reason: the candidate cannot approve readiness. Check that reviewers can distinguish preference, viewing and physical use; a prepared packet must support the full decision without the screen. Patron, librarian, service-owner and practitioner review must establish relevance, handling, formats and sustainable workload before later use. No operational approval is supplied.

## Tradeoffs and alternatives

Local dependency statements add reading but prevent hidden assumptions. Progressive detail may reduce burden while obscuring conditions, so essential limits stay visible. Optional comparison enables inspectable revision but adds state, privacy exposure and memory demands; review may remove it. Fixed choices avoid personal disclosure but omit possibilities, so unlisted and undecided outcomes remain valid.

Retain dissent: clearer notices, verified route information or removal of unnecessary account friction may solve the problem directly. A separately prepared static route board and packet are non-AI options. Conversation depends on an actually available person. Reviewers may choose these alternatives or stop development. Digital packet inspection alone is not equivalent offline delivery.

Complete invented paper/facilitation packet, to be independently prepared if paper practice is offered:

Card A — Notice and mission. “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Morning and afternoon sessions are offered; materials are provided in this example. Its notice says ‘Confirm your place.’ Explore a possible next step; nobody is registered. Use no personal information. Point, speak, mark, pass, pause or stop. Session preference: morning / afternoon / undecided; optional.”

Card B — Routes and authority. “Online practice describes an invented account step before confirmation; create no account and provide no details. Staff explanation depends on suitable assistance; real availability and language support are unknown. Paper practice depends on a complete usable prepared packet; real availability, format and service acceptance are unknown. Viewing content on a screen does not supply paper. No workable route and undecided are valid. You control continuing; the service owner controls requirements; providers control help and materials.”

Card C — Optional initial plan. “Route: online / staff explanation / paper preference / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect requirement / seek explanation if assistance exists / use a prepared packet if supplied / examine another route / wait without a promised duration / action not listed / undecided. Support preference: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: another route / undecided / pause / stop. Condition context: no hypothetical change / staff unavailable / packets exhausted / both.” Mark only if wanted. None selected does not establish no support needed.

Card D — Optional changes. “Imagine staff temporarily unavailable during this fictional visit. Your preference cannot make assistance available. Imagine prepared packets have run out. Viewing materials does not supply a physical packet; no printing or replenishment is arranged.” Choose either imagined condition, both or neither. Keep the preference unresolved, reconsider, wait without a promised duration, leave undecided, pause or stop. These are hypothetical changes, not reports.

Card E — Current plan. “Route: online / staff explanation / paper preference / no workable route / undecided. Next action: inspect requirement / seek explanation if assistance exists / use a prepared packet if supplied / examine another route / wait without a promised duration / action not listed / undecided. Support preference: explanation / reading aloud / language assistance / device assistance / none selected. Fallback: another route / undecided / pause / stop. Condition context: no hypothetical change / staff unavailable / packets exhausted / both. Physical supply, usable format and acceptance remain separate questions. Fictional plan; no registration or request sent.”

Card F — Correction, handling and facilitation. “Identify initial or current; replace the chosen mark or ask for a restatement. Initial choices retain their original condition context. An unrecorded initial plan stays unrecorded. Cancel leaves committed marks unchanged; no reason or score is required. Before marking, agree who may see the cards and how they will be handled. Unmarked participation is valid. Folding conceals; it does not erase.” Facilitator script: “Would you like to point, speak, mark, pass or stop? May I read the notice? Which route, if any? Would you like an imagined change? May I restate your choice so you can correct it?” Await explicit permission; collect no personal details, select no preferred answer and promise no provision.

Optional Story Circle card — “Neighborhood Story Circle is invented. Its notice says ‘Check joining arrangements’; arrangements remain unresolved and no account requirement is stated. Choose online notice inspection, conditional staff explanation, paper preference, no workable route or undecided. Use Cards C and E for choices, leaving Drawing Hour changes unused. Imagine shared-computer time ends; pause without replacing your preference. Correct, request detail, pass or stop. This is optional practice, not evidence of learning or transfer.”

Preparation note — Having this text does not establish physical supplies. Before offering paper practice, a human provider must prepare and inspect complete usable materials and handling arrangements. For the exhausted-supply scenario, use a separately prepared scenario card or oral delivery with an available facilitator; do not pretend the absent packet has been supplied.

## Acceptance checks

R1–R7 define proposed observable checks; none has run. Intended quality is a voluntary, manageable and correctable decision with honest dependencies. No implemented candidate or observed technical behavior is supplied here.

Technical verification must exercise correction, cancellation, replacement, concealment, clearing and reload, including focus, announcements and narrow/magnified layouts. Physical delivery verification separately requires the prepared packet; screen inspection cannot pass it. Passing any check establishes only the exercised behavior.

Human interaction review must examine wantedness, comprehension, refusal, language/format arrangements, privacy discoverability and provider burden. Learning, retention, transfer and flourishing require separate inquiry. Completion, speed, route revision or fewer prompts establish none of them.

## Evidence and unknowns

Sequence 15 supplies the integrated Design and its specialist lineage at sequences 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. Sequence 18 is the hypothetical review trigger. Sequence 2 preserves immutable parent context. These are draft and scenario evidence, not observations, approvals or executed checks.

Changed after sequence 18: paper viewing no longer implies screen-independent delivery; paper preference survives exhausted fictional supplies; initial/current plans retain supply context; human preparation and a separate physical-delivery check are explicit. Existing staff-dependency, correction, privacy and practice boundaries remain.

Unknowns include demand, actual routes, account necessity, packet supply and replenishment, usable formats, language arrangements, assistance, shared-device behavior and sustainable workload. Agency, dignity, access and belonging depend on actual participation conditions. Field pilot, learning, transfer and flourishing evidence remain pending.

## Next decision

Replace sequence 15’s Design brief with this bounded revision in response to sequence 18; do not rerun Understand or Map. Next, prepare paired screen-outline and independently provisioned packet review materials for pending patron, librarian, service-owner and accessibility-practitioner review. Preserve objections and corrections. Review may simplify comparison, select a non-AI service improvement, permit candidate development or stop. response.artifact_body:
The reviewed evidence is event 43, an actual Evaluate-stage host finding for artifact 35, SHA-256 eacb040c511d572b19b34572920944b0fffe55fcb01026f01dc29e9af1af4cfb. It follows revised Design 20 and Build revision 1. Sequence 32 describes an earlier artifact and bounded checks; it does not establish identity with this artifact. The preserved parent rehearsal at sequence 2 is background, not a measured baseline. This iteration requested Design, Build and Evaluate; this review neither reruns Instrument/Deploy nor records a pilot.

Three evidence levels must remain distinct. Source/packaging evidence comprises independent syntax checking, an offline stub/pure-state helper pass and reported integration/build checks. Those establish only their checked technical properties. Browser evidence comprises exercised behavior in the Codex in-app browser on macOS at 1280 × 720 with assistant-created fictional choices. Human task evidence is absent. No helper, build or browser result establishes comprehension, learning, scientific validity, service readiness or operational approval.

R1 and R2 connect patron choice with provider and service-owner authority. Interaction: select staff explanation or paper, then apply fictional unavailability or exhaustion. Purpose: preserve preference without inventing provision. Observable check: the choice persists, dependencies remain unresolved and no request, printing or replenishment is claimed. Event 43 observed these consequences and distinct before/current paper contexts. Sequence 18's hypothetical supply objection remains relevant: viewing materials does not supply physical paper. Event 43 rendered Cards A–F, facilitation permissions, Story Circle and readiness notes; print layout and independently supplied, screen-independent use remain untested.

R3 and R4 connect manageable inspection with contestable representation. Interaction: inspect the invented account condition, leave choices undecided, change or cancel a plan. Purpose: allow voluntary participation and faithful correction. Event 43 observed account inspection without account creation, current-editor cancellation and commitment of Language assistance as a preference while shortage persisted. Acceptance remains bounded to those exercised paths. Initial-editor correction, stale dependent wording across additional combinations and stopping without a completed plan require targeted checks. Before/now displays are representations of selected states, not measured improvement or a causal comparison.

R5 connects shared-device control with accessibility and privacy. Interaction: cover, reveal, resume, confirm or cancel clear, and reload. Purpose: separate visibility, activity and retained content. Event 43 observed cover pausing practice, reveal retaining pause, explicit resume, cancellation retaining cover, confirmed clearing removing plans without creating a draft, and reload restoring no prior choices. It also observed first Tab reaching Cover, no prohibited open-text/password/email fields in rendered DOM, no horizontal overflow at the reported width and no recorded console errors. These checks do not establish complete keyboard access, focus recovery, announcement behavior, magnification, narrow layouts or exhaustive absence of external activity. Pending-edit concealment/clearing and assistive-technology behavior need direct exercise.

R6 connects task distinction with the learning scientist's transfer boundary. Interaction: cancel or confirm replacement with Story Circle, then apply device-time ending. Purpose: prevent condition leakage and preserve preference during interruption. Event 43 observed cancellation retaining Drawing Hour, confirmed replacement removing prior plans and conditions, unresolved Story Circle arrangements without an account requirement, and device-time ending pausing practice while retaining online preference. This supports task separation in the exercised path. The second situation remains supported practice, with no retention or transfer evidence.

R7 connects human readiness with accountable alternatives. Before offering later participation, patron, librarian, service-owner and accessibility-practitioner review should examine wantedness, understandable dependencies, refusal, faithful representation, formats, languages, shared-device handling and workload. Inspect the complete independently prepared paper packet by conducting the full fictional decision without a screen. Preserve oral assistance where actually available, unmarked participation and stopping. Future review needs alone are not a current blocking defect.

For later measurement, use voluntary reviewed task evidence with documented assistance and condition context. Observe whether people can inspect a condition, express an acceptable next step and correct a misrepresentation; do not require online completion or infer understanding from silence. Include varied reading, language, device and access circumstances without patron scoring or deficit labels. No subgroup coverage exists now. Record reviewed findings in an agreed, privacy-preserving process rather than adding candidate telemetry.

Learning claims require a separate comparison and delayed task under documented support conditions. Transfer claims require a meaningfully changed task beyond repeated controls.
